fragments.text: Target edition: 17 October 2026. Gasket is a complete mobile CMMS for US maintenance teams replacing MaintainX, UpKeep or Fiix by Rockwell Automation and competing with Limble and Tractian. It keeps equipment available by turning faults, preventive requirements and live condition evidence into timely, resourced work, then preserving the technician evidence, spare-parts movements, purchasing, maintenance costs and reliability outcomes. It serves the full owned-equipment maintenance job, from one workshop to multiple plants and storerooms.

This is the product we are building towards. Missing implementation is engineering work, never a reduction of this destination. Every named clause states buyer behavior and acceptance through a public page, form, mobile app, JSON API, command, download or provider/gateway door. [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md) repeats every journey and its current status. The final Status section judges implementation at a pinned commit; local flow tests do not prove a hosted rollout, real vendor extraction, native app distribution or physical equipment safety.
| Category | Computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | MaintainX, UpKeep, Fiix by Rockwell Automation; Limble and Tractian |

| First buyer | A US maintenance lead at a small manufacturer, facilities operator or equipment-heavy business, with technicians, operators, a storeroom clerk, purchasing and an independent supervisor; USD costs and US operating norms |

An owner installation starts empty. Demonstration fixtures establish no live capability. The initial site, asset register, inspections, parts movements, independent review and agent-proposal guarantees below remain part of the full product; the prior single-site, Australian, manual-only and no-cost/no-offline/no-notification limits describe current gaps rather than target boundaries.
Every private handler authorizes current identity, role, site and record, including direct API calls, downloads and offline sync.
Required evidence and approvals are server rules. A contributor cannot approve their own work,
an agent cannot self-approve,
and a purchase initiator cannot authorize their own spend.
Source records, units, timestamps, corrections and human decisions remain attributable.
Automation is installation-owned, restart-safe, visible and stoppable; neither retries nor migration may create duplicate work, stock, bills or notices.

The scheduler's existing fixed-calendar and approval-reading meter cadence remains GAS-05's supported mode; PM-003 adds explicit buyer-selectable policies. Existing three-decimal quantities remain exact. Current 1.5 MB work evidence storage is an implementation limit to replace with declared target storage under ADMIN-008 and SAFE-003, not permission to discard source attachments.
**GAS-01 — Set up the site and its people.** The owner names the initial site and time zone, invites people as lead, maintainer, supervisor or agent, changes roles and ends access.
Every JSON, form, document and download handler enforces the current session and role; ending access revokes existing sessions.

New owner installations start empty. ADMIN-014 extends invitation and sign-in to people identified only by a mobile phone number, and ADMIN-015 adds Sign in with Google. **Acceptance evidence:** Through site and access pages and JSON/form doors, configure a site, invite and sign in each role, change one role and end access. Repeat private reads and writes signed out, forbidden and revoked; require refusal without leaked records.

**GAS-02 — Keep the asset register.** A lead records asset tag, name, serial, location, custodian, category, criticality and counter, gauge or condition meters with units. Edits retain earlier values. Sightings record found, elsewhere or missing; retirement preserves history and prevents new scheduled work. **Acceptance evidence:** Create and edit an asset through the register, add three meter types, record each sighting outcome and retire another asset. Read its previous identity and history; duplicate tags, stale edits and unauthorized changes are refused.

**GAS-03 — Keep the parts list and reconcile counts.** A lead keeps part numbers, names, units, stock locations and minimum quantities, receives stock and records physical counts. Counts post exact variance movements without rewriting receipts. Quantities are exact to three decimals; stale counts and invalid precision are refused. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive five units through the parts page, count four against the observed version, inspect the minus-one variance and retained receipt, then submit a stale count and excess precision through the API; neither changes stock.

**GAS-04 — Write checklists with revisions.** Leads create checklists and publish revisions. Issued work orders keep the exact procedure revision with which they were generated; editing the master never changes issued instructions or earlier results. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a checklist and issue a PM, publish a revision with an extra step, then open the issued work and revision history. Existing work retains its old steps and later work uses the new revision.

**GAS-05 — Schedule preventive work.** Leads define calendar intervals, counter intervals or both, first due date/value and default maintainer. The explicit Create due work orders command generates work due within seven days or at the counter threshold, with at most one open order per schedule. Automatic operation extends this guarantee in PM-001 and PM-002. **Acceptance evidence:** Create calendar and meter schedules through the API, cross each due boundary and request generation twice. Inspect one linked order per due schedule, the retained due value and no duplicate open work.

**GAS-06 — Assign work.** Leads create corrective work against an asset and assign or reassign work to active maintainers, leads or the owner; technicians also create and self-assign their own unplanned work under FIELD-009. Maintainers have their own work list; assigning a supervisor, agent, ended member or unknown person is refused. **Acceptance evidence:** Raise corrective work through the form door, assign and reassign it, then read both maintainers' own queues. Attempt each ineligible assignee through the JSON door and inspect unchanged assignment.

**GAS-07 — Capture the inspection.** The assigned maintainer records pass, fail or needs-attention results with notes, uploads photo or document evidence and records dated meter or condition readings. Other people cannot record the work. Backwards counter readings and future readings are refused; evidence downloads require access. **Acceptance evidence:** As the assigned technician, enter all result types, upload and download evidence, and record readings through work pages/API. Try another technician, a backwards counter and a future date; require refusal and retained original evidence.

**GAS-08 — Issue and return parts, record downtime and findings.** Assigned maintainers issue available parts, return no more than their holdings, record outage start and end with computed minutes, and record severity-coded findings. One asset has at most one open downtime. A finding requesting follow-up creates a linked corrective work order. **Acceptance evidence:** Issue and return parts through the work form/API, attempt excess stock and returns, open and close downtime, then request corrective follow-up from a finding. Inspect exact stock, minutes, linked work and refusal of overlapping open downtime.

**GAS-09 — Submit and review.** Submission requires all checklist results, a corrective finding linked to every failed or needs-attention result and closed downtime. Supervisors approve the exact reviewed version or return it with a reason. A person who performed work cannot approve it; stale review is refused. Approval closes work and advances the schedule. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit two failed steps with only one finding and require refusal, then supply linked findings and complete inspection evidence. Return with a reason, resubmit, attempt self-review and stale approval, and approve independently. Inspect retained reviews, closure and next schedule due point.

**GAS-10 — Watch overdue work and downtime.** Leads and supervisors see overdue work, work awaiting review, unresolved corrective follow-ups, assets down now, downtime minutes per asset over the last 30 days and stock below minimum. Open downtime contributes elapsed time; historic outages are clipped to the reporting window. **Acceptance evidence:** Open the board as lead and supervisor with overdue, submitted, failed and down assets plus low stock. Compare counts and clipped minutes with source records; a maintainer cannot read the board API.

**GAS-11 — Read and keep the history.** Members read asset work, results, readings, part movements, downtime, findings and reviews with actors and dates; leads and supervisors download the same history as CSV.
The owner exports the whole installation with rer export and restores it into a fresh installation with rer import without losing domain history.

**Acceptance evidence:** Read the full asset history and authorized CSV through public doors, compare events and attribution, export a populated installation using rer export, restore into an empty installation using rer import and compare domain records and attachment digests.

**GAS-12 — Move in from MaintainX.** The existing register importer accepts MaintainX asset, part and meter-reading CSV columns. A no-write preview lists creates, rejected rows and attention items; apply is bound to the reviewed fingerprint, journaled and idempotent. Undo removes only that import and refuses when later records depend on it. MIG-002 extends this to complete work history. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload the three CSVs through move-in, compare a no-write preview, refuse a changed fingerprint, apply and reapply, undo and import again. Create dependent Gasket records and verify undo reports blockers without removing data.

**GAS-13 — Let an agent prepare and a person approve.** An agent uses its own sign-in and the documented JSON API to read maintenance data and propose a schedule, corrective work or physical count. Proposals retain reasoning, payload hash and relied-on versions. A different lead or owner approves or rejects; approval executes the normal command atomically. Stale proposals and direct agent mutations are refused. **Acceptance evidence:** Sign in an agent, prepare each supported proposal via API, reject one, approve another as a different lead, change underlying stock and attempt stale approval. Try direct work capture, record mutation and self-approval; inspect refusals and attributed decisions.

**HTTP-001 — Health, Lobby and real 404s.** The installed origin serves the Lobby at /, deployment health and identity at /health, and real 404s for unknown HTTP and document routes. Private maintenance pages remain behind native sign-in. **Acceptance evidence:** Request the emitted Worker's root, health, unknown document, unknown API and health subpath; inspect branding, deployment identity and HTTP status, then attempt a private page signed out.

**ADMIN-001 — US operating defaults.** A US owner configures USD costs, US English as the organization's default display language (ADMIN-013 lets each person choose Spanish or another language), a US postal address and site time zones with daylight saving. Assets support customary and SI units with explicit conversions; schedules and reports show site-local dates and unambiguous timestamps. Existing data keeps its recorded units and currency. **Acceptance evidence:** Set up Ohio and Arizona sites, enter USD hourly rates and Fahrenheit/psi readings, cross a daylight-saving boundary and export. Verify due times, currency, unit labels and unchanged original readings.

**ADMIN-002 — Multiple sites and shared governance.** One organization manages sites, buildings, lines and storerooms with local calendars and shared asset/part standards. Owners delegate site managers; site membership scopes every list, attachment, report and write. Cross-site transfers retain identity and history. Reparenting a hierarchy entry (ASSET-001) under another site's parent needs management rights at both sites and is otherwise refused. The technician create-work right (FIELD-009) is turned off and on per site by its owner or site manager: that site's technicians are refused at every door while other sites' technicians still create work. The stores report (PART-009) filters by any site the reader may see. Before additional sites ship, this clause scopes REQ-001/REQ-002 portals, published targets and intake and REQ-003 queues, duplicate groups, source photos and work conversion to the authorized site. REPORT-006 multi-site authorization applies at every report, schedule, draft, preview, dispatch and download door before additional sites become operational. **Acceptance evidence:** Create two sites with distinct managers, move an asset with its meter history, then call each private door using the other site's member. Inspect denied access, correct local dates and organization rollups. As a manager of one site only, move a machine under the other site's line and see it refused (ASSET-001). Turn the technician create-work right off at one site and see that site's technicians refused at the web, API and app doors while the other site's technicians still create work (FIELD-009).

**ADMIN-003 — Role rights and separation of duties.** Owner controls identity, integrations and retention; site admin manages that site; lead plans/assigns and manages registers; technician creates corrective and emergency work, including work already completed, against assets and locations (FIELD-009) and records assigned or self-assigned work; supervisor reviews independently; storeroom clerk counts/issues/receives, and a stores supervisor independently approves count variances (PART-004); buyer drafts POs; purchasing approver authorizes spend; analyst reads authorized reports. Permission templates and custom grants keep work creation, execution, approval and cost-rate visibility separate. Create work is a default technician right that an owner or site admin revokes per role and site, and a ready-made Operator template sees and records only work assigned to that person. Broader delegated scheduling rights inherited from REPORT-006 must preserve current report and export permissions, attributable preparation, explicit owner authorization of the saved revision and separation of preparation from outbound authority. **Acceptance evidence:** Sign in each role and exercise its permitted public doors, including direct forbidden writes/exports. Add a custom site-scoped role, revoke it and test old sessions; technician work and purchasing cannot be self-approved. Remove create work from the technician role at one site and see that site's technicians refused at app and API while the other site's technicians still create work; give a person the Operator template and see only their assigned work.

**ADMIN-004 — Requester and contractor access.** Requesters and contractors are invited by mobile phone number or email address (ADMIN-014); neither needs a company email. Requesters submit and follow their own faults without seeing private maintenance costs or other people's requests. Contractors receive expiring access to named work, instructions and evidence, record completion and costs, and cannot browse the asset estate or approve their work. Neither ever reads the team's internal comments or their photos (PLAN-006). Requesters and contractors never create work orders at any door (FIELD-009); they use request intake (REQ-001, REQ-002). **Acceptance evidence:** Invite a requester by US mobile number only and an external electrician by email, have the requester sign in with a one-time SMS code, submit a fault and follow it, and finish assigned contractor work. Change URL/API identifiers to other records, inspect denied access, expire the contractor grant and test its active session. The requester and the contractor are refused a work order's and an asset's internal comments and comment photos (PLAN-006) by URL and API. A requester and a contractor are refused work creation at the web, API and app doors (FIELD-009).

**ADMIN-005 — Enterprise identity lifecycle.** Microsoft Entra ID and Okta SAML/OIDC SSO, enforced MFA policy and SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning map organization groups to site roles. Owner recovery is audited; deprovisioning ends browser, API and mobile access, including queued offline writes at sync. The same applies to people who sign in by phone number (ADMIN-014): ending a phone-only person's access, or changing their number, ends their app sessions and offline sync. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect each identity provider at its network edge, provision two site groups, require MFA, deprovision an active technician and attempt web/API/offline sync. Repeat for a phone-only technician with queued offline work: end their access and attempt app sync. Inspect refusal of every attempt and a logged owner recovery.

**ADMIN-006 — Attributed append-only audit.** Maintenance changes, immutable readings and movements, checklist revisions, reviews and import decisions commit atomically with actor, action, record and time. Owners and authorized supervisors search/export audit by site, action and date, including integration and AI decisions; corrections append rather than rewrite evidence. While an installation holds one site (until ADMIN-002), the site filter of audit search and export accepts that one site and refuses any other with 404, and every entry and CSV row names its site; per-site attribution across several sites grows with ADMIN-002. **Acceptance evidence:** Perform work, count, review and import through public doors, trigger a stale write, and inspect the audit download. The failed write adds no business change; previous readings remain visible and integration/AI actions name their authority. Filter search and export by the installation's site and by another site id (404); every entry and CSV row names its site.

**ADMIN-007 — Retention and verifiable erasure.** Owners set retention and legal holds for attachments, request contacts, users and maintenance records. An erasure preview identifies dependencies and retained obligations; apply removes eligible records/files, anonymizes retained audit, and produces a per-type result. Later restores honor the erasure journal; recipients' prior downloads remain outside local erasure. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a held work record and an eligible requester/photo, preview and apply erasure through the owner door, inspect bytes and anonymized audit, and restore an older archive with the later erasure journal. Held records remain and erased records do not reappear.

**ADMIN-008 — Protected credentials and private attachments.** Provider tokens, sensor certificates and mobile credentials are encrypted under installation authority, narrowly scoped, rotatable and revocable.
Private file access rechecks current record rights;

original attachments use Cloudflare R2 or owner object storage with resumable uploads, declared limits, malware handling and safe rendering. Telemetry aggregation runs in bounded background jobs rather than long request-time database scans. Logs, exports and AI context redact secrets; disconnecting a provider stops new sends. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect/rotate/revoke a provider, upload a private manual and hostile file, then use unauthorized, expired and cross-site download links. Export and inspect logs/context for planted secrets; revoked connectors produce no new outbound requests.

**ADMIN-009 — Complete portable archive and inactive restore.** Owners download a documented archive of all sites, assets, work/history, PMs, requests, stock/movements, POs, costs, attachments, audit and import mappings with schema versions, counts and digests. Restore into empty data validates before writes, pauses automation and excludes sessions/provider secrets; owners reconnect services deliberately. **Acceptance evidence:** Export a realistic multi-site estate through the supported command/download, interrupt/resume, validate digests and restore to a fresh installation. Compare every record class; corrupt and nonempty restores write nothing and restored PMs do not send or buy.

**ADMIN-010 — Backup recovery and connector operations.** The owner sees backup freshness, last successful restore drill, background-worker and connector lag, failed jobs, quotas and actionable failures. Recovery preserves accepted work and notification/purchasing idempotency; an operator can pause a failing automation without deleting its history. **Acceptance evidence:** Back up populated data, interrupt a PM/receipt job, recover to another installation and reconnect intentionally. Inspect visible recovery point, job errors and deduplicated resumed work through owner operations pages.

**ADMIN-011 — Accessible responsive maintenance workspace.** Core setup, intake, planning, stores, reporting and work execution are usable at 1440 and 390 widths with keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, visible focus and text status. Long asset names and errors remain readable; failed saves keep entered work and disclose whether it was persisted. **Acceptance evidence:** Use every core journey at 1440 and 390 with realistic long records, keyboard and assistive semantics. Induce a save failure, reload the confirmed record and inspect retained draft, focus, text errors and absence of horizontal clipping.

**ADMIN-012 — Search, saved views and bulk maintenance actions.** People search/filter assets, work, requests, procedures, parts and vendors by tag, serial, site, owner, date, status and custom fields. Saved views and permission-aware bulk edit/assign/export show a preview and per-record failures; pagination never silently omits the estate. **Acceptance evidence:** Find a serial among thousands of assets, save a cross-filtered view, bulk reassign selected work including a forbidden record and export all pages. Inspect exact selection, denial and totals.

**ADMIN-013 — Per-person display language.** Owners set the organization's default display language and every person (owner, lead, technician, supervisor, stores, purchasing, requester, contractor) chooses their own. US English and US Spanish ship complete at launch; the published catalog covers at least 30 display languages, including French, Portuguese, Vietnamese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Korean, Tagalog, Polish and right-to-left Arabic. The chosen language applies to the web workspace, the iOS and Android app (FIELD-001), the requester portal and QR fault form (REQ-001, REQ-002), email and push notices (PM-005, INT-004), printed work packs (FIELD-008) and PDF reports (REPORT-006). Signed-out requesters get the portal's site default or their browser preference and can switch. Dates and numbers follow the person's locale while stored values, units, USD amounts and timestamps are unchanged. User-entered text (asset names, checklist steps, notes, readings, comments) is shown exactly as authored, and translated procedures come only from AGENT-007's reviewed translations. A missing translation shows the English string with a visible untranslated marker, never a blank control, and owners can download a per-language completeness report. The existing operator portal and scoped QR form under REQ-001/REQ-002 inherit this full obligation: complete language catalogs, person/site/browser preference, locale formatting and visible fallback must be asserted at both current intake doors by this clause before its language support ships. Localized scheduled report packs inherited from REPORT-006 follow this per-person language and locale duty while preserving stored source values and authored text. **Acceptance evidence:** Set the organization default to English and one technician and one requester to Spanish. On the technician's phone app, the requester's QR fault form and portal, an emailed and a push notification, and a printed work pack, show interface text in Spanish while user-entered checklist text, readings, units, USD amounts and audit attribution stay byte-for-byte unchanged and an English lead still sees English. Remove one Spanish catalog string and show the visible English fallback marker, not a blank control, plus the completeness report naming it. Switch a user to Arabic and check right-to-left layout at 390 width without clipping.

**ADMIN-014 — Phone-number invites and SMS sign-in.** An owner, site admin or lead invites any person (technician, supervisor, storeroom clerk, buyer, requester or contractor) by mobile phone number or by email address; neither is required. A phone invite is a text message, sent through the owner's connected SMS provider (Twilio or Amazon SNS), with an expiring single-use acceptance link. The person then signs in to the web workspace and the iOS and Android app (FIELD-001) with a six-digit one-time code sent by SMS and valid for 10 minutes. Numbers are stored in E.164 form and identify one person in the organization. Duplicate numbers, malformed numbers and numbers in countries the owner has not enabled (the US and Canada at launch) are refused with a visible reason. A number that has opted out by replying STOP is shown as unreachable rather than silently retried. Code requests are limited to five per number in 15 minutes and per network address, five wrong codes lock the number for 15 minutes, and codes never appear in logs, exports or AI context. A person can add an email address later. Changing a number requires a code sent to the new number. Changing the number or ending access revokes every existing web and app session, API token and device grant, and the person's queued offline writes are refused at sync with a per-record reason that stays visible to them and their lead (FIELD-003). Invitations, code requests, sign-ins, number changes and opt-outs appear in the audit (ADMIN-006). SMS delivery status is visible on the invitation, and provider acceptance never counts as acceptance by the person. Imported users with only a phone number become phone-identified invitations mapped to their history (MIG-002, MIG-008). **Acceptance evidence:** (1) Invite a technician by US mobile number only and inspect the SMS invitation at the provider edge. (2) Accept it, sign in to the iOS and Android app with the one-time SMS code, and receive and complete assigned work. (3) Invite a requester the same way and follow their own request. (4) Import a MaintainX user export containing a phone-only user and see that user mapped to their completed work. (5) Submit a duplicate number, a malformed number and a number from a country that is not enabled, and see each refused with a visible reason. (6) Request a sixth code within 15 minutes and see it refused with a retry time, then enter five wrong codes and see the lockout. (7) Change one phone-only technician's number and end another's access while both hold queued offline work, then sync: existing sessions are revoked, every queued write is refused with a visible reason, and the audit records each event.

**ADMIN-015 — Sign in with Google.** Owners enable Sign in with Google for the organization, optionally limited to named Google Workspace domains, alongside email-link, SMS (ADMIN-014) and enterprise SSO (ADMIN-005) sign-in. A Google account signs in only when its verified email matches an invited or active member, unless the owner sets a domain rule that admits new members at a named default role for review. Members can link and unlink Google from their profile, and owners can require Google or SSO sign-in for owners and leads. Ending access in Gasket revokes existing sessions regardless of the Google session, and the provider credentials are protected under ADMIN-008. **Acceptance evidence:** Enable Google with test credentials at the network edge, sign in an invited lead with Google and land on their own work, and see an uninvited Google account and an account outside the allowed Workspace domain refused. Unlink Google and sign in by email link, require Google for leads and see an email-link lead sign-in refused, then end the lead's access and see their Google sign-in refused and their active session revoked.

**ADMIN-016 — User and full maintenance-record erasure.** The unfinished user and full maintenance-record erasure portion of ADMIN-007 remains a separate obligation. Owner-confirmed erasure must respect retention, legal holds and retained evidence obligations, preserve anonymized audit and prevent resurrection on later restore.

**ASSET-001 — Asset and location hierarchy.** Leads model site/building/line/machine/component parentage with stable identifiers and locations. Moving a subtree preserves work and rolls cost/downtime up without counting an outage twice; cycles and cross-site unauthorized reparenting are refused.

Exactly: the site is the root; under it every register entry is a building, line, machine or component, and keeps its id and tag through every move. A parent ranks above its child in that order (a component may also hold components), is active, and is never the entry itself or anything below it; a stale read, a parent of the wrong level, a retired parent and a cycle are refused and write nothing, and an entry with active entries below it cannot be retired. Leads (and the owner) place an entry when they register it and move it later; moving an entry takes everything below it along, work, downtime, readings and history stay on the entries they were recorded on, and the move shows in the history of the entry and of both parents. An entry's roll-up covers it and everything below it: open work, ended downtime as the union of their outages so an outage they share counts once (the shared minutes are shown; entries down now are listed and their outage counts once it ends, as on each asset), and moved-in work cost (MIG-002) in parts, labor and other. Done covers the one site and the cost records that exist today; ADMIN-002 refuses reparenting across sites without rights at both, REPORT-001 rolls its work costs up this hierarchy, and MIG-001 places imported assets under the parents their source names, each before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a compressor under a line, move its component subtree and open parent history/report totals. Attempt a cycle and cross-site move; verify refused writes and retained descendant records.

**ASSET-002 — QR and barcode identification.** Leads print durable QR and barcode labels for assets, locations and bins. Scanning with a phone camera or supported scanner opens the authorized record, the scoped fault form (REQ-002) or, for a member with the create-work right, new work against that asset or location (FIELD-009); a public label never grants private work/history access. Reprints preserve identity. The code is the existing explicitly published target identity; leads and owners print it, while the owner configures which display name may be public under REQ-001. An active signed-out scan opens only its scoped intake; a member scan offers the authorized record and the ordinary create-work door if the current site grants it. Retired targets reprint the same code and refuse new faults/work with an explicit retired state; unknown codes are explicit 404s. A bin label identifies its published bin location today; PART-001 inherits its stock-bin record link before bin balances ship. FIELD-001 carries native scanner deep links before its app ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Print asset and location labels, scan at a technician phone and signed-out operator portal, report a fault against a location label with no asset, reprint a retired asset label and scan an unknown code. Inspect correct route, restricted fields and explicit retired/unknown states.

**ASSET-003 — Manuals, documents and warranties.** Assets hold versioned OEM manuals, diagrams, warranties, supplier contacts, commissioning dates and authorized documents with expiry reminders. Technicians see the version linked to issued work; offline packs include approved files and retain original attribution. A document is a manual, diagram, warranty, authorization (permit, licence or certificate) or other document of one asset, kept as numbered revisions of a PDF, image or plain-text file of up to 1.5 MB that never change or go away; each revision names its source (publisher and reference) and who added it when. Leads (and the owner) add documents, revisions and contacts; adding a revision, from the revision the lead read (a stale one is refused), is its approval and makes it the master. A lead links a document to open work on the same asset, pinning the current revision or a named earlier one; the work shows and packs that revision, marked when the master has moved on, until a lead links it again. The job pack is one ZIP download of the work order's summary, the pinned files unchanged and a manifest of each file's document, revision, original name, source, SHA-256 and who added it; FIELD-002's offline packs inherit the same pinned files and attribution before they ship. An expiring document names an active member as its owner and reminder days (0 to 365, default 30): on a scheduler run (PM-001) the owner gets one in-app notice once the site's day is within that many days before the expiry date and one more on or after it, and a changed date asks again; email and push wait for PM-005. Supplier, manufacturer and service contacts, each with a phone or email, are kept on the asset; commissioning dates are ASSET-007's lifecycle facts. **Acceptance evidence:** Attach two manual revisions, link one to work, set a warranty expiration and download the job pack. Change the master and inspect issued/offline documents plus the named owner's expiry reminder.

**ASSET-004 — Status, criticality and failure taxonomy.** Asset states distinguish available, degraded, down, out of service and retired; criticality, risk, failure mode, cause and remedy codes are maintained centrally and mapped on imports. A status change keeps its effective time and reason; manual and telemetry disagreement is visible. The catalog is one site-wide list per kind: criticality is an ordered list of levels (seeded Normal, Important, Critical) that leads add to, reorder, relabel and retire, and risk, failure mode, cause and remedy codes are maintained the same way. A code's key never changes; every record keeps the code it was given, a retired code stays readable on it and is no longer given to new records or matched by imports. An imported value maps onto the active code whose key, label or one of its import names equals it, ignoring case; a value that matches none is refused for criticality and moves in unclassified, with an attention item, for a failure code. Findings carry optional failure mode, cause, remedy and risk codes, and the failure report counts findings and moved-in work by code, lists what is unclassified and names the assets whose evidence disagrees with their declared state. Done covers every importer that exists today (MaintainX criticality and work categories); each later importer (MIG-001 through MIG-008) maps the codes its source carries this way before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Take a critical pump down, correct its outage classification and map an imported failure code. Inspect effective status history and unclassified/contradictory evidence in reports without rewriting the original event.

**ASSET-005 — Meters, units and counter corrections.** Meters record source time, receipt time, unit, quality and provenance for counter/gauge/condition readings. Reset, replacement, rollover and corrected readings require an explained append-only adjustment; stale or suspect readings cannot silently fire PMs or reverse counters. Staleness is per meter feed: each meter declares a feed window in whole hours (1 to 168, 24 by default; a daily-cadence feed can declare 36), and a feed reading received more than that window after its source time is stale. Manual readings, attested by the person who took them on a work order, are not aged. A reading keeps the quality it was received with when the window later changes, and creating due work lists the schedules that stale or suspect readings hold back. **Acceptance evidence:** Enter manual readings then a replacement counter and late/corrected feed through public doors. Compare normalized run hours, quality flags and due work, and attempt an unexplained backwards reading.

**ASSET-006 — Bill of materials and interchangeable spares.** Each asset/component has a revisioned bill of materials, required quantities, approved substitutes, compatible serial/model ranges and linked tools. Work planning sees stock at eligible storerooms and warns when a substitute is not approved.

Exactly: a lead or owner saves an asset's bill of materials as numbered revisions, never rewriting an earlier one (a stale revision number is refused): lines of parts with the quantity a repair needs and an optional serial range the line fits, approved alternate parts per line each with its own optional serial range, and the tools the work needs, named. Serial ranges include both ends and compare in natural order (digit runs as numbers, letters ignoring case); an asset without a serial fits only lines and alternates without a range. The asset page and every work order on the asset show the current revision with each part's and alternate's available stock (PART-002), whether it fits the asset's serial and which lines are short, and earlier revisions stay listed. Reserving (PART-002) accepts an alternate the current revision lists for that line only when it fits the asset's serial, otherwise a site-wide approved substitute, and refuses with a visible reason a part or alternate outside its serial range or a substitute neither approves; that refusal is the warning. Done covers what exists today: one storeroom per site, assets without component parentage, tools as names and serial numbers as the only compatibility attribute; ASSET-001 gives components their own revisions, PART-001 shows stock per eligible storeroom, PLAN-004 links the named tools to its tool register and ASSET-009 adds model ranges once a model field exists, each before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a motor BOM with two approved bearings and a serial restriction, plan a repair with one out of stock and select a substitute. Inspect compatibility and quantities on the resulting work/parts reservation.

**ASSET-007 — Asset lifecycle and replacement decision.** Leads record purchase, commissioning, warranty, service agreement, replacement value and retirement/disposal with retained service history. A replacement comparison uses actual maintenance cost and downtime; accounting depreciation remains in the connected ledger. Money is US dollars kept in whole cents; purchase and commissioning dates are not in the future and commissioning is not before purchase; a replacement value names its basis; a service agreement has a provider, scope and term (end not before start) and is active from its first to its last day inclusive in the site's calendar. Each lifecycle change is a numbered revision (a stale one is refused) recorded in the asset's history, and a retired asset's facts no longer change. Retiring records the disposal (sold, scrapped, returned, transferred, donated or other, its date and optional proceeds). The comparison's repair cost is the sum of every cost entry (REPORT-005) on the asset's own work orders in any status, unknown (never zero) when there are none; its downtime is the minutes of the asset's ended failure stops by their latest classification (REPORT-003); the repair cost is shown as a percentage of the replacement value to one decimal. The ledger handoff is a CSV of these facts and costs to date with no book value or depreciation. **Acceptance evidence:** Import an older asset, record its purchase and service agreement, compare repair cost with replacement value and retire it. Open its history and export the ledger handoff without deleting prior work.

**ASSET-008 — Inspections, rounds and calibration.** Leads publish multi-asset inspection routes and calibration tasks with due tolerances, required tools, certificate attachments and failed-reading follow-up. Each stop records its asset and procedure revision; missed or failed stops stay open independently.

A route is an ordered list of at least two stops, each an asset and the checklist done there; issuing it makes a run with one work order per stop, all due the same day and pinned to each checklist's current revision, so a failed reading (FIELD-004) raises its follow-up on that stop alone. A missed stop keeps its reason and stays open; a supervisor (the review right) signs a run off only once every stop is closed, so signing never closes missing work. A route may repeat every N whole days from its first due date (fixed cadence, to a default person): the scheduler (PM-001) and Create due work orders issue one run per occurrence (`route@date`) once its date is within the site's lead time, whatever state earlier runs are in, and a route with a retired stop waits. A route or schedule may name required tools; each work order it issues lists them, and its submission waits until the person doing it records which one was used (a serial or asset number).

A calibration task is a schedule on an instrument whose procedure carries the tolerances: its number steps with inclusive limits (FIELD-004), at least one required, so a reading outside them fails and needs a linked finding with follow-up work. Its due tolerance is a grace window of 0 to 90 whole days after the due date, in the site's time zone: the task reads in date before the due date, due through due date + grace, overdue after; its cadence runs from the day its work is approved unless the lead chooses fixed (PM-003). Its work needs a certificate (an attached PDF or image marked as the certificate) before review; approval keeps the latest certificate as the instrument's next certificate version with the procedure revision, the tools used, whether it was on time (approved by due date + grace) and its result: out of tolerance when any number step failed, in tolerance otherwise. That result is Gasket's reading of the recorded values against the procedure's limits; Gasket does not certify the instrument or verify the reference standard's own certification. Earlier versions are kept. A tool register with its own calibration due dates and booking is PLAN-004's, and compliance template libraries, qualification links and audit packs are SAFE-002's, each owed to calibration tasks before it ships.

**Acceptance evidence:** Schedule a route across three assets and a gauge calibration, fail one reading and skip one stop. Inspect independent follow-up, calibration certificate/version and incomplete route state; signing a route cannot close missing work.

**ASSET-009 — Custom asset and part fields.** Leads define typed custom fields on assets, locations and parts (text, number with unit, single or multiple choice, date, yes/no and link), scoped to the organization, a site or an asset or part category, and mark each required or optional with validation. Values show and edit on register pages, the technician app and the QR scan view, and are available in search, filters and saved views (ADMIN-012), automation conditions (PLAN-009), dashboards (REPORT-007), the API (INT-001), imports (MIG-001, MIG-002, MIG-007) and every export. Value changes keep history with actor and time. Renaming a field keeps its values; retiring a field archives its values instead of deleting them. **Acceptance evidence:** Define a required "Refrigerant type" choice field on the HVAC asset category and a "Voltage" number field in volts on parts. Set values through the register and the app, read them back on the page, the QR scan view and the API, filter assets by refrigerant type and export CSV with the values. An invalid choice and a missing required value are refused. Rename one field and retire another, then inspect retained values and history. Import a MaintainX asset export with a custom-field column and see it mapped onto the field.

**REQ-001 — Web operator request portal.** Operators submit faults from a branded web portal against a selected asset/location with description, urgency, contact and attachments, plus the site's own request fields: administrators configure per-site or per-portal text, choice, number, date and photo fields, mark them required or optional and map them onto the request. The portal shows in the requester's display language (ADMIN-013). ADMIN-013 carries complete catalogs, per-person and organization preferences, signed-out browser/site language selection, locale formatting and visible English fallback for both this portal and REQ-002's QR form before that language door ships; its acceptance journey must exercise both existing intake doors. Until ADMIN-002 adds sites, a portal belongs to the installation's current site. Intake defaults to active signed-in human members; ADMIN-004 inherits requester/contractor identities and their own-request-only access before those identities ship. An owner explicitly audits opening bounded public intake and publishing each opaque target's display name; a public form never lists targets or exposes private asset names, history, costs or request records. Contacts are as given, never verified identities. The adopted conservative default is five new submissions per portal/network/hour and 100 per installation/hour, content-validated PNG or JPEG photos up to 1.5 MB each and five per request, with EXIF and GPS metadata stripped before hashing and storage, and a receipt capability containing only the saved request number. Ct approved these defaults on 23 October 2026 at 08:42Z with riders: limit refusals return explicit errors and are logged without personal data; explicit owner-confirmed erasure removes contacts, photos and details, including copied corrective fault details. Administrators choose authenticated or bounded public intake; anonymous access is rate-limited and cannot enumerate private assets. **Acceptance evidence:** Add a required "Is the line stopped?" choice to one site's form, then submit a noisy-motor fault with a photo through signed-in and public configured intake and see the answer on the request; omit the required field and see refusal. Test invalid asset, file limit and abuse controls, then inspect a persisted request and private-data refusal.

**REQ-002 — QR mobile fault reporting.** An operator scans an asset QR code to open a phone fault form, in their display language (ADMIN-013), prefilled with allowed asset identity. ADMIN-013 carries this existing form's complete display-language catalog, signed-out selection, locale formatting and visible fallback before its language door ships, and exercises this form in its own acceptance journey. It supports camera evidence and saved drafts with visible submission confirmation; repeated submit and reconnect creates one request. Ct approved explicit device-storage opt-in on 23 October 2026 at 08:42Z: drafts stay on that device, confirmation clears private contents retaining only the receipt, and sign-out clears drafts across open tabs and fences stale saves. **Acceptance evidence:** At 390 width scan the pump label, photograph a leak, lose connectivity before sending and reconnect/retry. Inspect exactly one request, original asset mapping and a durable confirmation.

**REQ-003 — Triage, duplicate linking and corrective conversion.** Leads triage requests by site, asset criticality, urgency and impact, ask for details, link duplicates, approve/decline with a reason and convert to corrective work without retyping. The original requester, photos and timeline stay linked. Existing leads and owners triage their current installation site, recording production impact (unknown, running, reduced or stopped); ADMIN-002 inherits cross-site queue scoping before additional sites ship. Every decision has a reason and the version seen. Duplicate links stay a one-level group for the same asset or location, retaining every report. Approval permits conversion, not automatic spending or dispatch; conversion uses the original target, description and urgency and is atomic with source links, so retries return the existing work. Questions/replies remain attributed on the request timeline; REQ-004 inherits external requester conversations and delivery before those doors ship. Only planners/reviewers and the work's current assignee/collaborators receive its necessary linked fault/photo evidence; private contacts stay on the creator/lead request door. **Acceptance evidence:** Triage two reports of the same fault, request more details, link one as duplicate and create one corrective order. Open both request timelines and work evidence; reject a third with an explained outcome.

**REQ-004 — Requester status and two-way updates.** Requesters see submitted, acknowledged, planned, waiting, resolved or declined status for their own reports and exchange scoped comments/photos. Actual email/push delivery follows configured events; resolution links the completion summary while hiding rates, private notes and other requests. The requester conversation is its own; the team's internal comments on the work order and asset (PLAN-006) never appear in it. REQ-003 currently records attributable questions, replies and decisions on request timelines; this clause inherits their requester conversation/delivery under own-request scope before those external doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit as an operator, receive acknowledgment, reply with a photo, observe a waiting-on-parts update and then a technician resolution. Inspect mailbox/push edge and portal privacy using another requester, and see none of the work order's internal comments (PLAN-006) in the portal.

**REQ-005 — Response targets and escalation.** Leads define acknowledgment and resolution targets by priority and site calendar, with accountable owners and after-hours rules. Unacknowledged or overdue requests escalate to named people, and paused clocks require an explicit reason rather than disappearing from backlog. Current clocks pin the priority policy, site time zone, weekday hours and holiday snapshot at submission. After-hours policy either counts all elapsed time or only open site hours. Acknowledgment uses the first retained triage decision; resolution ends at linked work closure or an explicit decline, abandonment or duplicate decision. Reasoned pause and resume events exclude only their interval and never hide the request. The existing owner-controlled chase job records one in-app escalation per overdue clock with named ownership, input evidence and grant revision; acknowledgment stops further acknowledgment escalation, while resolution remains independent. PM-005 inherits external delivery and ADMIN-002 inherits additional site scope. Ct ruled: only active owners and leads within triage access can be accountable owners or escalation recipients; inactive accounts and other recipients are denied without additional request data exposure. REQ-008 carries the named gap Escalation to assigned staff and groups, with ADMIN-004 requester groups and ADMIN-002 site scope; ADMIN-003 inherits future role routing. **Acceptance evidence:** Create urgent and routine requests before a site holiday, advance the clock, pause one for access and inspect distinct target clocks, overdue notices and escalation ownership until acknowledged.

**REQ-006 — Email and Google Forms intake.** A site inbound email address accepts fault descriptions, attachments and replies with sender validation; Google Forms responses map authorized asset/location fields into requests through a documented connector. Message/response IDs deduplicate repeated deliveries; rejected rows are visible. **Acceptance evidence:** Send an operator email and replay a Google Forms response at the network edge, reply to the acknowledgment and submit an unmappable asset. Inspect one request per source ID, linked reply and actionable rejection.

**REQ-007 — Request reporting and operator adoption.** Leads see request volumes, acknowledgment and resolution time, repeat faults, conversion and rejection reasons by site, asset and requester group. Reports link to the exact records and show untriaged and abandoned requests rather than excluding them from response metrics. Current lead and owner triage permission protects the page, JSON and CSV doors. The current installation is the site dimension; ADMIN-002 inherits authorized multi-site report scoping before more sites ship. Requester groups describe signed-in intake, public unverified intake and erased identity; ADMIN-004 inherits future requester groups under its scoped identities. Acknowledgment is the first recorded lead decision on each report; resolution is independent closure of linked corrective work. Declines stay separate from repair resolution. Durations disclose elapsed totals, measured counts, missing counts and all-request counts. Repeat faults are explicit duplicate links; conversion counts reports linked by retained work-created events, with the canonical approval reason. Abandonment is an explicit reasoned triage decision that retains the report, never an inference from waiting time. Erased sources remain counted with unavailable identity and timeline evidence disclosed. REPORT-009 definitions, retained omissions, source links and freshness apply to all these measures. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit, duplicate, decline, convert and leave requests untriaged, then filter and download the request dashboard and compare counts and time denominators with source timestamps.

**REQ-008 — Escalation to assigned staff and groups.** Extend request escalation beyond the active owner and lead slice to assigned staff and groups within authorized triage access. This missing scope inherits ADMIN-004 requester groups and ADMIN-002 site scope; unauthorized recipients receive no request data.

**PLAN-001 — Priority, lifecycle and reusable work templates.** Leads plan corrective, emergency and preventive work against an asset or a location with no asset (a restroom door, a dock light) with priority, estimated duration, instructions, due date, custom fields and permissioned custom statuses. Reusable templates and bulk creation preserve stable work numbers and required completion/review rules. Work a technician creates (FIELD-009) follows the same template, required-field, required-evidence and review rules as work a lead creates. A work order names exactly one asset or, with no asset, one location: the text the lead gives, trimmed, up to 160 characters, with the site's known asset and work locations offered; its follow-ups keep the location, and downtime and meter readings, which belong to an asset, are refused on it; preventive work at a location comes from a calendar schedule naming that location, since meters belong to assets. A custom field is text, a number or one of two to thirty listed choices; one marked required needs a value before any work order is submitted for review under its current definition (so it binds open work too, and a retired field never does), and a template may also require fields and photo or document evidence, kept with the work made from that revision. A waiting status (for example Waiting on parts) sits inside the lifecycle on open work and names the roles (lead, maintainer, supervisor; the owner always) that may set or clear it; a maintainer sets one only on work they hold or collaborate on. **Acceptance evidence:** Create urgent corrective work from a template, create location-only work for a dock light, add a required field and custom waiting status, bulk-create selected jobs and try to bypass completion requirements through the API as a lead and as the technician who created the work. Inspect persistent numbers and refusal.

**PLAN-002 — Teams, trades and accountable assignments.** A work order has an accountable assignee plus collaborators, trade/team and shift. Leads assign/reassign with handoff notes; technicians acknowledge or decline with a blocker and only authorized participants record scoped work. A team is a named group of assignable people (owner, leads, maintainers) with one trade, kept by leads; a work order may name a team, a trade (the team's by default) and a shift label, and when it names a team every assignment door (assign, overdue plan, bulk) gives it only to a member of that team. Every reassignment keeps a handoff (from and to person and shift, an optional note, who and when) and asks the new assignee to acknowledge again. Collaborators are assignable people a lead adds or removes; the assignee and active collaborators record results, readings, evidence, parts, downtime and findings, only the assignee acknowledges, declines, answers chasing and submits, and anyone else is refused. Declining needs a blocker (PM-006's kinds, owner, next action and promised date), returns the work unassigned and gives every active lead (the owners when there is none) an in-app notice; PM-005 adds email and push delivery of it before it ships. Each record names who made it, the work order lists its contributors, and a contributor cannot review it (GAS-09). **Acceptance evidence:** Assign an electrical job to a team and lead technician, add a collaborator and hand over across shifts. Inspect both queues, acknowledgment and recorded contributor; an unrelated technician cannot write.

**PLAN-003 — Calendar and workload scheduling.** Leads schedule work on day and week calendars with estimated hours, preview when dragging or rescheduling and capacity by person/team/site. Workload conflicts, unassigned jobs, leave and overdue work remain visible; calendar edits do not silently reset PM due policy. Slots are separate from original due dates and estimates: moving or removing a slot leaves the PM occurrence and cadence unchanged. Explicit person windows supply capacity; overlapping absence reduces the denominator. Existing assignment and handoff doors release incompatible bookings when the accountable person changes. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule five repairs into a 16-hour team window, mark a technician absent and move a job between days. Inspect capacity and conflicts, unassigned work and unchanged PM due evidence on desktop and phone.

**PLAN-004 — Skills, qualifications and resources.** Planning matches required trades, certifications, availability, tools and reserved parts; expired qualifications or double-booked resources block or require an authorized recorded exception. Utilization separates assigned, productive and unavailable hours. The current planning door matches trades through team membership, dated qualification references, explicit availability, named work and BOM tools linked to the calibrated tool register, and BOM quantities held through parts reservations. It rechecks constraints on confirmation; subsequent absence, expiry and physical stock shortages remain visible as conflicts. Assigned hours are active slots; productive hours are approved wrench time, excluding travel, wait, administrative and legacy unclassified time. Capacity is explicit availability minus overlapping absence, with no inferred workday.

Ct approves these supported defaults with riders: only the owner creates, edits or retires qualification records and tool records, including tool identity and calibration facts. Retirement preserves attributed history and prevents retired records from satisfying new requirements. Planning reads, availability edits and resource use require the existing work assignment right and existing record access; they do not grant record-maintenance rights, unrestricted personnel access, private certificate originals, personal identifiers, private contacts, pay rates or unrelated records. Source documents retain their separate access controls.

A certification or licence reference is information the owner entered, not verification by Gasket with an issuing body. Every reference display identifies it as “Owner-entered reference — not verified by Gasket with the issuing body,” with recorded dates and calculated expiry distinguished from verification. Gasket does not certify competence, physical safety, trade licensing, legal compliance or employment-law compliance. Qualified people choose applicable standards and authorize physical maintenance and equipment release.

A hard block refuses planning confirmation or assignment when a required qualification or tool is missing, expired, unavailable or incompatibly booked. No override is supported. Gap: Broader qualification and tool-record role grants remain required under PLAN-004 and ADMIN-003. Gap: Authorized recorded exceptions remain part of the target and require a separately authorized approver, reason, attributable audit, explicit scope and expiry before shipping. Gap: Automatic qualification expiry and renewal reminders are unproved; existing document expiry reminders remain under ASSET-003 and external notification delivery under PM-005.

Qualification data can be personal data. Corrections and retirement preserve attributed prior evidence under ADMIN-006; retirement is not erasure. Retention, legal holds, eligible erasure, anonymized retained audit and prevention of resurrection on restore remain under ADMIN-007 and ADMIN-016. Complete archive and inactive restore coverage remain under ADMIN-009 and GAS-11. Gap: Qualification-specific audit, erasure, retention and restore coverage is unproved by this policy review.

SAFE-001 inherits qualification references for qualified sign-offs, prerequisites, expiry and changed-evidence reapproval; SAFE-002 inherits training and qualification links, retained certificates and complete portable compliance audit packs. ADMIN-002 inherits site-scoped access at every door before additional sites ship. ASSET-006 and ASSET-008 retain linked tool-register, calibration, booking and tool-use obligations. All unproved obligations remain named Gaps without reducing the complete target.

**Acceptance evidence:** Plan a high-voltage repair for a technician with an expired credential and a shared tool already booked. Resolve both constraints and inspect the schedulable slot and utilization denominator.

**PLAN-005 — Dependencies and production windows.** Work can depend on predecessor jobs, equipment access, permits, parts and approved production shutdown windows. Planning exposes the critical blockers and coordinates with the buyer's production calendar; moving a window retains the original promise and alerts affected owners. **Acceptance evidence:** Plan a repair after isolation and parts receipt in a production window, move that window from the connected calendar and inspect blocked/ready states and affected owner notices.

**PLAN-006 — Comments, mentions and shift handoff.** Authorized teams use work/asset comments, photos, mentions and handoff summaries with read/unread state and durable notification links. Internal notes stay private from requesters/contractors; edits retain history and resolution does not delete the conversation. Conversations not tied to a record are PLAN-008.

Exactly: every member who can read a work order or an asset reads its comments, in the order they were posted; the owner, leads, maintainers and supervisors post them and an agent does not. A comment is text of up to 2,000 characters with up to four photos (PNG, JPEG, WebP or HEIC, up to 1.5 MB each), may be marked a shift handoff summary, and mentions active people chosen when it is posted; each mentioned person gets one in-app notice on the Notices page that links to the comment on its record. Only its author edits a comment and every version stays readable with who and when; no door deletes a comment, so approving, canceling or merging the record keeps its conversation, which can continue. A comment someone else wrote is unread for a person until they open the record's page or mark its thread read through the JSON door; an edit never makes a read comment unread, and a mention notice is unread until its comment is read. Every comment is an internal note. Done covers the identities that exist today (owner, lead, maintainer, supervisor and agent, all internal); requester and contractor access (ADMIN-004) and the requester conversation (REQ-004) keep these comments and their photos from requesters and contractors before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Mention the incoming technician on a returning job with a photo and internal cost note, sign in on their phone and follow the notice. Inspect unread state, retained edit history and contractor/requester privacy.

**PLAN-007 — Bulk actions and controlled cancellation.** Leads bulk assign, reschedule or cancel selected work after seeing affected dependencies and PM consequences: until PLAN-005 work dependencies exist, each selected row shows its schedule consequence and open follow-up work, and PLAN-005 adds dependency consequences. Bulk operations through the JSON door (`workorders.bulk`, a preview then per-row outcomes) satisfy the bulk operation itself; bulk selection on the Work page remains a requirement, delivered with the owner-chosen Work table look. Merge, reopen and skip-occurrence live on the work-order and schedules pages. Reopening a returned repair means a reviewed, closed corrective repair whose fault came back reopens to Returned for rework and fresh review; canceled work reopens to Open. Cancellation, reopening and merging duplicate work retain reasons, original evidence and links; partial failures are reported per item and cannot fabricate completed maintenance. **Acceptance evidence:** Select mixed authorized/stale work, preview a bulk reschedule (each row shows its schedule consequence and open follow-up work) and cancel one PM, then reopen a reviewed, closed corrective repair whose fault came back and see it Returned for rework and fresh review, and reopen canceled work to Open. Inspect per-row outcomes, retained evidence and an overdue PM obligation until explicitly resolved. Select several rows on the Work page and apply a bulk action there.

**PLAN-008 — Team, group and direct messaging.** Members hold one-to-one, ad-hoc group and team conversations plus a site-wide All team conversation in the web workspace and the iOS and Android app, with no Slack or Teams subscription required. Creating a team creates its conversation; joining a team grants it and leaving or removal ends access to every message sent afterwards. Messages carry text, photos, files, record links and mentions, with unread counts, read state, deep links and push/email notices under each person's preferences (PM-005). A person with work-creation rights (technicians by default, ADMIN-003 and FIELD-009) turns a message into a request or corrective work that links back to the message and keeps its photos as original, attributed evidence. Messages written offline queue on the device and send exactly once after reconnecting. Requesters and contractors never see internal conversations. Edits and deletions keep history, owners can apply retention and legal hold (ADMIN-007), and conversations are included in audit export (ADMIN-006) and the portable archive (ADMIN-009). **Acceptance evidence:** Create a team and confirm its conversation appears for current members and for a member added later. Send a one-to-one message and a group message with a photo between a technician's phone and a lead's browser; inspect push delivery at the APNs/FCM edge, deep-link opening and unread/read state. Turn one message into corrective work that links back to the message and keeps the original photo digest. Queue a message offline, reconnect twice and see it delivered once. Remove a member and verify app and API refuse messages sent after removal; a requester and a contractor are refused internal conversations by URL and API.

**PLAN-009 — No-code automation rules.** Leads build site-scoped rules without code from documented triggers (request submitted, work created or changed status, asset status changed, meter reading recorded, part below minimum, checklist result failed, work overdue) with conditions on asset, location, category, priority, team, custom field and time of day, and actions (route or assign to a team or person, set priority, status or due date, attach a procedure, notify people or a channel, create follow-up work, request approval). Rules are versioned, can be tested against recent records without changing anything, run in a stated order with conflicts shown, are loop-protected and pausable, and record the rule revision on every action. Actions run within the rule owner's rights and can never approve work, approve spend or close a finding. **Acceptance evidence:** Build a rule that routes new requests for Line 2 conveyors to the electrical team at high priority, test it against last week's requests with no changes written, then enable it and submit one matching and one non-matching request. Inspect the assignment, the rule revision in audit and no action on the non-match. Create two rules that would trigger each other and see the loop stopped with a visible error; save a rule whose action approves work and see it refused.

**PM-001 — Unattended calendar generation.** An installation-owned scheduler generates recurring calendar PMs without a person pressing a button, using each site's time zone, lead time and fixed- or completion-based policy. Each due occurrence has a stable identity; restart, overlap and retry create one work order and retain missed-run debt. The scheduler is a Cron Trigger every 15 minutes (UTC), declared for the deployed Worker and run by `rer dev`; each run issues, at the site's time zone, calendar work the site's lead time ahead of its due date (whole days, 0 to 90, 7 by default; the owner sets it on the Site page or through `site.configure`) and counter or trigger work as soon as it is due (PM-002, PM-003). Manual generation uses the same lead time. Gasket keeps one site per installation today, so each installation's site has its own lead time; ADMIN-002 inherits a lead time per site before it ships. An occurrence is its schedule plus its due date (or counter value, or triggering reading); the scheduler never issues an occurrence that already had a work order, so a canceled occurrence stays owed until a person reissues or skips it. Every run is kept; a run more than 45 minutes after the one before records the gap, and calendar work the scheduler issued after its due date is listed as issued late, on the Schedules page and in `scheduler`. **Acceptance evidence:** Save a monthly PM through the schedule door, leave the app, cross its due window and restart the scheduler twice. Open one generated order, its due occurrence and any missed-run warning without invoking manual generation.

**PM-002 — Automatic meter and condition triggers.** Validated manual or integrated counter, gauge and condition readings automatically evaluate thresholds, trend duration and hysteresis. Combined calendar/meter policies state whichever-first or both; repeated/late sensor deliveries do not duplicate work or satisfy a condition with stale data. Every reading a door keeps (a feed reading or one taken on a work order) evaluates the schedules on its meter at once. A gauge trigger fires when good readings stay strictly above (or below) its threshold and a condition trigger when they stay in its chosen conditions, for at least its sustain minutes measured between source times (0: the first such reading); after firing it re-arms only once a later good reading is at or past its reset value (the threshold unless set; for a condition, out of the chosen conditions). Only good readings received after the trigger was set up count, so stale, suspect, moved-in or earlier readings never fire one. A counter is due at its value. A schedule with a calendar and a meter is due on whichever comes first unless it states both. A feed delivery repeating a kept reading (same meter, feed, source time and value) is that reading, not a new one, and a schedule never has more than one open order. Generated work names the reading that raised it. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure counter and sustained-temperature triggers, send fresh, repeated, late and recovered readings through ingest and await generated work. Inspect one order per trigger, source evidence and explicit rejection of stale data.

**PM-003 — Cadence, seasonal windows and exceptions.** Leads choose fixed versus completion cadence, seasonal months, weekdays, holidays, shutdown windows and bounded deferral with a reason. Skipping a task retains the missed obligation and independent risk approval; editing schedules previews already-issued and future work. Due dates are site-local calendar days, so a daylight-saving change never moves one. A calendar schedule may allow only some months and ISO weekdays and, unless it is set to run through them, avoids the site's closures (holidays and shutdown windows, both ends inclusive, kept by leads); a due date on a day it may not fall moves forward to the next allowed day, never earlier. Fixed cadence counts from the planned (nominal) date, so moves never drift it; completion cadence counts from the day the work is approved. A lead asks to skip an overdue occurrence that has no open work, or to defer the current occurrence to a date after it and at most the schedule's deferral limit later (14 days unless set, up to 365), always with a reason; nothing moves until an owner or supervisor other than the person who asked approves it (on a site with one owner and no supervisor, that owner may approve their own request after an explicit second confirmation, and the decision is labeled single-approver), issued work moves with an approved deferral and keeps its checklist revision, and every request and decision stays on record, so a skipped occurrence remains recorded as missed. Editing a calendar schedule's interval, cadence or calendar shows a no-write preview of its issued work (unchanged: due date and checklist revision) and of its next five due dates before and after the change. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure weekday/seasonal PMs across a holiday and daylight-saving change, defer one with approval and edit an interval. Inspect next dates, retained missed work and unchanged issued checklist/due evidence.

**PM-004 — Failed inspection creates accountable correction.** A failed required result automatically creates or links a corrective finding/work order according to a lead-approved rule, carrying failed step, readings, evidence, severity and deadline. A lead-approved rule is one numbered rule per checklist (outcomes, severity, due days) that a lead or owner sets, revised by appending a new number. The correction goes to the inspection's assignee, who must acknowledge it before submitting, and only an independent approval of the correction resolves the original failure; closing the PM cannot hide unresolved corrective work. The notice is in-app: the correction on its assignee's own list and on the board, plus the audit entry; email and APNs/FCM delivery of it belongs to PM-005. **Acceptance evidence:** Fail a required inspection item through mobile/API without manually asking for follow-up, inspect the linked corrective work and its in-app notice (the assignee's list, the board and the audit entry), see submission refused until the assignee acknowledges, complete/review it and verify the originating failure closes only under the checklist's numbered rule and only on an independent approval.

**PM-005 — Assignee and approver notifications.** Generation, assignment, returned work, review request and due changes enqueue actual email and APNs/FCM mobile push to authorized people with record links. Each event/destination has delivery status, deduplication, per-person channel/event preferences and quiet hours, and escalation when delivery fails; notices render in each recipient's display language (ADMIN-013), and provider acceptance is distinct from human acknowledgment. Owners can mark an escalation mandatory so preferences cannot suppress it. **Acceptance evidence:** Generate and return work, inspect email and mobile push at provider edges, open the deep link and acknowledge. Turn off a technician's email for assignment events while keeping push and set quiet hours, assign work and inspect push delivered, email suppressed with the preference recorded as the reason, and a mandatory escalation still delivered during quiet hours. Induce a delivery failure and retry/restart; inspect visible failure and no duplicated business event.

**PM-006 — Overdue escalation and blocker chasing.** Rules remind the accountable technician before/after due time, request an acknowledgment/blocker, and escalate to the lead and supervisor on elapsed thresholds or missing response. Parts, access, skill and production blockers have owners and next actions; reassigning needs a lead decision and never resets age. Chasing runs with the scheduler (PM-001) on the site's dates under one lead-approved rule (revisions kept; by default remind one day before the due date, expect a response within one day of the overdue notice, escalate to leads after two days overdue and to supervisors after five): the assignee is reminded the set days before the due date and again once it is overdue and answers on it or blocked; every active lead is notified once the work has been overdue for the lead days or the assignee has not responded within the response days after the overdue notice, and every active supervisor (the owners when there is none) after the supervisor days. A blocker names its kind, owner (any active member, the reporter by default), next action and promised date; a promise not cleared by its date notifies its owner and the leads. Each notice goes once per recipient and occasion and is an in-app notice on the Notices page and the work order; PM-005 adds email and push delivery of these notices before it ships. Overdue age counts from the day the work first became overdue and no reassignment or reschedule resets it. **Acceptance evidence:** Leave urgent PM unacknowledged, advance the clock, report a parts blocker and miss its promised date. Inspect escalating notices, accountable blocker and approved reassignment while the original overdue age remains.

**PM-007 — PM template rollout and change control.** Leads version preventive strategies across asset classes/sites, preview affected schedules, preserve local overrides and obtain required approval for revised safety/OEM requirements. Rollout never silently rewrites issued work; cancellation and catch-up plans are explicit. Gasket ships a versioned library of ready-made procedure and PM templates for common equipment (air compressors, pumps, electric motors, conveyors, HVAC units, boilers, forklifts, fire extinguishers and backup generators) that leads copy, adapt and approve before use; a copied template keeps a link to its library version. **Acceptance evidence:** Copy the library air-compressor template, adapt and approve it, then publish a revised compressor program to two sites with one local override, review the diff and approve rollout. Inspect future schedules, unchanged issued work and a conflict requiring local decision.

**PM-008 — Scheduler health and automation controls.** Owners see last/next run, due-event coverage, paused rules, delivery backlog and per-job errors. They can test a rule without live work/purchases, pause/resume and safely catch up; workers have bounded authority and all automatic actions retain rule revision and input evidence.
