Exactly: the Automation page and JSON doors show the last scheduler trigger, the next UTC quarter-hour trigger, current calendar/meter due-event coverage and the latest executions. The owner pauses or resumes each current automatic job (PM generation, inspection routes, work chasing and document-expiry reminders) with a reason and numbered grant revision, pauses or enables an individual PM schedule with its revision, and runs catch-up under the revision they saw. Pausing retains due dates, issued work and source records; a last successful job more than 45 minutes ago is visibly missed even while paused. A read-only preview of a PM schedule, paused or enabled, uses the ordinary due evaluator but writes no work, notices, purchasing records, audit or execution rows. Each attempted job records its source (cron, reading or catch-up), grant revision, input facts, start, end and completed, paused or failed outcome; stale catch-up is a retained failure with no work. Automatic work audit entries and notices reference that job and its revision; PM work also keeps its schedule revision and due occurrence or reading, routes keep their stops, chasing its numbered rule, and document reminders their expiry facts. Automatic writes recheck the current unpaused grant in their transaction. The owner cannot use a job name to authorize reviews, spend or unrelated actions. The current notice jobs save in-app notices synchronously; their running and failed job counts are shown, while external email/push delivery is explicitly unavailable, never a zero provider backlog or an invented send. Done covers every automatic capability that exists today (PM-001, PM-002, PM-006, ASSET-003, ASSET-008, PART-005 and BUY-006 vendor follow-up, whose reminder email outcomes are shown): PM-005/INT-004 add actual external delivery backlog and failures, PLAN-009 rules, INT-002 through INT-017 connector jobs and AGENT-001 through AGENT-009 autonomous jobs inherit these preview, control, authority, provenance and health obligations before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Test then enable a PM rule, stop its worker across a due slot and inspect a visible missed-run condition. Resume/catch up and inspect one due work order with rule revision; test mode sends no live notification.

**PM-009 — Nested and coordinated preventive programs.** Leads define nested PM packages so an approved higher-level service can satisfy explicitly mapped lower-level tasks, coordinate linked assets and avoid duplicate downtime. Suppression records the exact task/revision/occurrence evidence and never hides an overdue obligation without the approved equivalent work.

Exactly: leads publish numbered, immutable task mappings between higher and lower schedules, including schedules on linked assets, with a reason for the equivalence. Every lower task maps to a higher task of the same type, unit, limits and choices; the mapping pins both procedure revisions and cycles are refused. On the Programs page a lead previews and applies a specific pair of occurrences with the same due day. The higher work must be independently approved and closed; each mapped task needs a passing result or its required photo, never an exception or an unanswered, failed or conditional non-applicable task. The lower work must still be untouched and open. A missing mapped task leaves that occurrence and its due date unchanged. Applying the equivalent records both work versions, procedure revisions, mapping revision, review and original result/photo references, retains the lower work as cancelled with a visible satisfaction link (never as separately performed maintenance), releases its reservations and advances only its schedule by its ordinary cadence. A satisfied occurrence cannot be reopened or applied twice; later mapping or procedure revisions do not rewrite earlier satisfaction evidence. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule weekly, monthly and annual nested services, complete an annual package with one mapped task missing and inspect lower-level obligations. Only fully evidenced approved equivalents suppress duplicate work; missed steps stay due.

**FIELD-001 — iOS and Android technician app.** Installable iOS and Android apps provide secure sign-in (email link, one-time SMS code for people known only by mobile number under ADMIN-014, Google under ADMIN-015 or organization SSO under ADMIN-005), own/team work, creating new corrective work and logging completed work (FIELD-009), asset scan, manuals, team messaging (PLAN-008) and notifications with deep links, in each person's display language (ADMIN-013). Supported OS/device versions and release/update requirements are published; a browser-only page does not establish native offline or push delivery. The app is a create-work door under FIELD-009 and carries its obligations before it ships: a technician scans an asset QR label (ASSET-002) and creates corrective work with priority, description and a photo, takes it or leaves it unassigned for a lead, and sees it in their own queue and on the lead's board; a template's required field and required photo are refused exactly as at the API; app-created work is recorded with the door `app`; and requesters, contractors and technicians whose create-work right is off are refused. The app's checklists carry FIELD-004 before it ships: typed steps with units and limits, conditional steps, a photo on its step, a supervisor's exception with its reason, and submission blocked exactly as at the API. **Acceptance evidence:** Install release builds on an iPhone and Android phone, sign in one technician by email link and a phone-only technician with a one-time SMS code, scan an asset and create corrective work against it, open an assigned job from push and update the app while retaining authorized drafts. On the app, scan an asset QR label, create corrective work with priority, description and a photo, assign it to yourself and see it in your own queue and on the lead's board; omit a template's required field and photo and see the API's refusal; see the audit record the door `app`; a requester, a contractor and a technician whose site has the create-work right off are refused (FIELD-009).

**FIELD-002 — Offline work packs and durable capture.** Technicians download authorized jobs, procedures, asset history, parts availability snapshots and manuals before losing service. Checklist results, readings, notes, photos, signatures, time and part usage persist through airplane mode, app termination and device restart; unsynced state and stale stock are explicit. New work a technician creates offline (FIELD-009) is a durable draft with a device-local identity that syncs exactly once and receives its server work number on reconnect. Work created offline is recorded with the door `sync` (FIELD-009). Offline checklists keep FIELD-004's typed steps: conditions evaluate on the device, a number's outcome comes from its limits, a step photo stays bound to its step through sync, and the server's submission blockers apply on reconnect. Photos, annotations and signatures captured offline keep FIELD-005's phase, capture time, version binding and stale-signature rule, and record the door `sync`. Manuals in an offline pack are the document revisions pinned on the work (ASSET-003), each with its source and who added it, never a later master. **Acceptance evidence:** Download a job, enter airplane mode, record every evidence type, kill/restart the app and reopen the draft. Create a new corrective work order with a photo in airplane mode, restart the device, reconnect twice and see exactly one work order with one server number. Verify all bytes/times survive, stock is labeled a snapshot and the app shows what remains unsynced. The audit records the synced work order's creator and the door `sync` (FIELD-009).

**FIELD-003 — Reconnection, conflicts and device revocation.** Reconnect sync is resumable and idempotent with per-record results. Server-side assignment, stock, meter and review versions remain authoritative; conflicting offline changes need a visible resolution and never disappear. Revoked users/devices cannot upload; remote wipe policy and local-data expiry are disclosed. Work created offline whose creator's create-work right or access ended before it syncs is refused at sync with a visible per-record reason that stays on the device and in the lead's view (FIELD-009). **Acceptance evidence:** Two devices edit the same job offline and consume the last part, then reconnect in reverse order and interrupt photo sync. Inspect one accepted movement, visible conflict and retained draft; revoke a device and verify refused upload. Create work in airplane mode, revoke the creator's create-work right before reconnecting, sync, and see the work refused with a visible reason that stays on the device and the lead's view (FIELD-009).

**FIELD-004 — Typed checklists and required evidence.** Procedures support pass/fail, numbers with limits/units, text, options, required photos, conditional steps and required readings. A failed tolerance links to follow-up; supervisor-controlled exceptions require a reason, and procedure changes keep historical step identities. A step is a check (pass, needs attention or fail), a number with its unit and inclusive limits (either limit may be left open) that passes inside them and fails outside, text, a choice from listed options where the options marked to fail fail, or a required photo (an image attached to that step; a document does not answer it). A step may apply only when an earlier step has a named answer (an option's value, otherwise its outcome); a step that does not apply takes no answer and blocks nothing. A number step may name the asset meter it reads, which must have the same unit; its value is then kept as that meter's manual reading (ASSET-005), so required readings are number steps. Before submission a failed limit needs a linked finding with follow-up work (raised by hand or as a PM-004 correction), and a failed or needs-attention check or option needs a linked finding. A supervisor, meaning anyone with the review right (owner or supervisor) who recorded nothing on the work, may grant an exception on one applicable step with a reason; it is kept unchanged and the step then blocks nothing. Each step has a key: a new revision keeps a step's key when the step keeps its label (ignoring case) or names its earlier key, and issued work keeps the revision it was created with. Today's doors are the web workspace (on a phone browser too) and the JSON API; the native app (FIELD-001) and offline capture (FIELD-002) carry these step kinds, conditions, step photos, exceptions and blocked submission before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish a checklist with conditional temperature and photo steps, fail a limit and try to submit with missing required evidence through phone and API. Inspect blocked submission, linked finding and retained step revision.

**FIELD-005 — Photos, annotations and signatures.** Technicians capture timestamped before/after photos, annotate damage, attach documents and collect named technician/customer or supervisor signatures tied to the exact work revision. Original files/digests survive edits and sync; signature capture never claims equipment certification.

Exactly: evidence may be marked before or after the work and carry the time it was taken (site local time, never ahead of now) besides its upload time, and records the door it came through (`web` or `api`; offline capture is `sync` under FIELD-002). An annotation is a box, ellipse or arrow placed in percent of a photo's width and height (two decimals) with a note, drawn over the photo where its pixel size is known (PNG, JPEG); the original file and its SHA-256 never change. A technician signature is given by the assignee or a collaborator as themselves (the signed-in member); a customer signature is recorded on that person's session by the name the customer gives, with an optional drawn mark kept with its SHA-256, and is labelled as a name as given, not verified; a supervisor signature is given by a member with the review right who did no work on it, on submitted work, for the version they review. Every signature binds to the work order's version at signing and never changes the work; signing any other version is refused as stale. Any later change to the work makes technician and customer signatures stale, and submission waits until each such signer signs the current version; earlier signatures stay on record as superseded. A signature confirms the work record at that version and is labelled as not an equipment certification. FIELD-002 and FIELD-003 carry offline capture, offline signatures and upload provenance under these same rules before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Capture/annotate two photos, obtain a named signature, change the work and submit a stale signature. Download originals and inspect revision binding, required re-signing and offline upload provenance.

**FIELD-006 — Wrench time, labor and contractor costs.** Technicians start, pause and resume timers and enter corrected time with reasons, distinguishing wrench time, travel, wait and admin by person and work. Overlap and implausible duration need review; authorized labor rates, overtime policy and contractor charges cost work without exposing pay rates to unauthorized roles. **Acceptance evidence:** Record two technicians' timed work and a contractor invoice, cross midnight, correct a timer and attempt overlap. Inspect approved hours and USD costs on work and asset reports, with rates hidden from a requester. Current implementation semantic (ct approved 23 October 2026): the owner manages rates, overtime, invoice capture and time decisions; technicians submit and read their own source entries. Every entry needs a reasoned review, with overlaps and durations over 16 hours flagged. Timers submit separate elapsed segments when paused or stopped; paused gaps contribute no time. Corrections retain the original and replace it only when approved. Approval snapshots the latest authorized rate and splits elapsed time at each site midnight; each day uses its remaining regular-time allowance after other approved time, then the overtime multiplier. A later rate or correction never reprices other approved snapshots. Existing report readers receive aggregate approved time and work costs; person-level cost and pay policy remain owner-only, and audit details contain no pay rate. Overtime is a configurable review policy, not a legal wage calculation; no payroll data is transmitted. ADMIN-002 and ADMIN-003 inherit the same source and rate privacy when site scope and delegated rights ship; FIELD-002 and FIELD-003 inherit retained segments and approval semantics when offline time ships. Original work-minute notes retain author attribution but declare no performer, interval, category or approval; they remain separately disclosed evidence, never guessed person time or pay. REPORT-010 carries approved person time under these privacy rights before it is done.

**FIELD-007 — Crew completion and independent review.** Multi-person work records each contributor and required step sign-off, supports blocked/in-progress/returned states and independent supervisor review. Reassignment preserves contributors, so no one who performed any step can approve; material changes require fresh review. Contributors are the assignee and collaborators (PLAN-002); each checklist step keeps who signed it off, and every step needs a result before submission. Work is blocked while it carries an open owned blocker (PM-006) or a waiting status (PLAN-001), and stays in progress meanwhile. Anyone who recorded a step result, reading, part movement, downtime, finding or evidence on the work, whoever holds it now, is refused approval. Every record makes a new revision of the work; submitted work takes no records until it is returned, and an approval names the exact revision it read (an older one is refused as stale). **Acceptance evidence:** Complete a repair with two technicians, reassign to a third, submit and attempt review by each contributor. Require independent approval of the exact final revision and retain the return/rework history.

**FIELD-008 — Field usability, print and secure device lifecycle.** Phone execution provides glove-usable controls of at least 48 by 48 CSS pixels with at least 8 pixels between targets, camera/scanner support, accessible instructions and explicit save/sync feedback; printable work packs retain IDs/revisions for controlled later entry. Shared-device sign-out protects cached data, and lost devices can be revoked without deleting server history. **Acceptance evidence:** Use a job at 390 width with long instructions and measure every interactive control at no less than 48 by 48 CSS pixels with 8 pixels spacing, print a pack, re-enter its evidence with provenance, sign out a shared device and revoke another. Inspect cache isolation and intact server records.

**FIELD-009 — Technician-created and after-the-fact work.** Technicians create their own unplanned work from the iOS and Android app (FIELD-001), the web workspace and the JSON API; it is a default right of the technician role (ADMIN-003) that an owner or site admin revokes per site. A technician opens new corrective or emergency work against a scanned asset (ASSET-002), a picked asset or a location with no asset (PLAN-001), with priority, description, photos and an optional template, then assigns it to themselves or leaves it unassigned on the lead's board. They can also record work already done: past start and end times, parts issued (PART-003), a closed downtime (GAS-08) and a checklist from a template. Technician-created work keeps a stable work number and follows the same template, required-field, required-evidence and stock rules as lead-created work (PLAN-001, FIELD-004). It goes to independent supervisor review (GAS-09, FIELD-007), and its creator, like any contributor, cannot approve it. Work created offline (FIELD-002) syncs exactly once; if the creator's create-work right or access ended meanwhile it is refused at sync with a visible per-record reason (FIELD-003, ADMIN-014). Requesters, contractors and roles without the right are refused at every door and use request intake (REQ-001, REQ-002) instead. The creator, the door used (app, web, API or offline sync) and the time are recorded in the audit (ADMIN-006), and technician-created work counts in backlog, MTTR and downtime reporting (REPORT-003, REPORT-005) exactly like other work. Until site admins exist (ADMIN-002/003) the owner turns the right off and on for the site; while it is off every create door refuses a technician, and a follow-up raised by a finding on work they hold (GAS-08) is not technician-created work. The door is recorded as `web` (the workspace's form door) or `api` (the JSON API); FIELD-001 adds `app` and FIELD-002 `sync`. Past start and end are site-local minutes, given together, with start no later than end and end no later than the site's clock; a template's checklist is pinned at the revision current when the work is created. Doors and identities that do not exist yet carry these obligations in their own text and acceptance before they ship: the app and QR scan (FIELD-001, ASSET-002), offline creation with exactly-once sync and refusal at sync (FIELD-002, FIELD-003), per-site revocation across sites (ADMIN-002) and requester and contractor refusal (ADMIN-004). **Acceptance evidence:** (1) On the iOS and Android app, a technician scans an asset QR label and creates corrective work with priority, description and a photo, assigns it to themselves, and sees it in their own queue and on the lead's board. (2) The technician records work already done with a past start and end time, parts issued, a closed downtime and a checklist from a template; it goes to independent supervisor review and the creator's approval is refused. (3) Omit a required template field and required photo evidence on technician-created work through the app and the API and see the same refusal a lead gets. (4) An owner removes the create-work right from the technician role at one site; that site's technicians are refused at the app and the API while technicians at the other site still create work. (5) A requester and a contractor are refused at the same app and API doors. (6) Open the backlog, MTTR and downtime reports and the audit download, and see the technician-created work counted, with its creator and door attributed. (7) Create work in airplane mode, revoke the creator's right before reconnecting, sync, and see the work refused with a visible reason that stays on the device and the lead's view. Point (1), the app half of (3), the second site of (4), the requester and contractor of (5) and point (7) are asserted under FIELD-001, ADMIN-002, ADMIN-004, FIELD-002 and FIELD-003, which carry them.

**PART-001 — Multi-location stock and bin visibility.** Stores staff see on-hand, reserved, available, on-order and in-transit quantities per site/storeroom/bin with barcode lookup and units. Reorder and issue decisions use available stock; site permissions govern transfers and reads. Stock value and average cost (PART-007) are kept per site, storeroom and bin, and cycle counts (PART-004) are planned and counted by bin. ASSET-002 supplies published bin-location labels today; when this clause adds stock-bin records, their scans must open the authorized stock-bin record without expanding public access. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive the same bearing into two sites and three bins, reserve one quantity and scan a bin. Compare available/on-hand/on-order totals and attempt an unauthorized cross-site read.

**PART-002 — Parts reservations, kits and approved substitution.** Planners reserve parts or repair kits to work before dispatch, allocating across bins and approved substitutes. Reservations expire/release on cancellation; competing work cannot reserve the same last unit. Physical issue remains a separate movement.

Exactly: a lead or owner approves one part as a substitute for another (that direction only) and can withdraw the approval, and keeps repair kits, each a named fixed set of parts and quantities (a different mix is a new kit). A planner (lead or owner) reserves to open work one part, or every line of a kit at once, each line filled by the part it names or by an approved substitute for it, never an unapproved one; a work order holds at most one open reservation per part, and a kit is reserved whole or not at all. A part's reserved stock is, over its open reservations, what each still needs (its quantity less what its work order has been issued of that part, net of returns, never below zero), and available is on hand less reserved; a reservation is refused unless every part it touches stays at or above zero available, checked in the same atomic write, so competing work cannot reserve the same last unit, and issuing to work never takes stock reserved for other work. A physical count can still leave a part short, shown as negative available. A reservation ends, kept with who ended it, when and why, when a planner releases it with a reason or when its work order is canceled, merged into another or approved and closed; reservations do not lapse by time. Reserving never moves stock: on hand changes only by receipt, issue, return and count. Gasket keeps one shelf location per part and one site today; PART-001 allocates reservations across bins and storerooms and ADMIN-002 across sites before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Reserve a repair kit to two competing work orders, substitute an approved part and cancel one order. Inspect exact available stock, released reservation and unchanged physical on-hand until issue.

**PART-003 — Controlled issues, returns and traceability.** Issues/returns identify work, asset, person, bin, quantity and effective time; lot/serial/expiry tracking is available for controlled spares. Returns preserve original issue value, quarantine damaged items and never exceed holdings; a damaged work return credits the work at its retained issue value and records an equal, separate quarantine adjustment, excluded from usable stock and available value until disposition. A reason is required and the current return form defaults to usable; offline conflicts require explicit resolution. Expiring lots appear in the stores report (PART-009). The current web and JSON doors require an explicit receipt source and stable request identity for controlled issues; a serial is one whole unit. Recorded expiry permits issue through that site-local date and refuses later dates. Usable returns and inspected releases retain their source. Historical unattributed issues and count variances refuse affected controlled stock pending bin reconciliation under PART-001. FIELD-002 inherits offline reconciliation. **Acceptance evidence:** Issue a serialized spare from a named bin, return one damaged item and attempt an excess return/replayed offline issue. Inspect linked movements, quarantine quantity, original valuation and duplicate refusal.

**PART-004 — Cycle counts and inventory adjustments.** Stores staff plan blind counts by bin, freeze or reconcile concurrent movements and submit variances for configured independent approval. Each approved adjustment appends an attributed movement; lost, found and damaged stock have reason codes and cost effect.

Exactly: a lead or the owner plans a count of one shelf location's parts and/or chosen parts for one counter (an active owner, lead or maintainer); the count sheet never shows its counter the expected quantity while the count is open (the parts register still shows on-hand to its readers). Gasket reconciles rather than freezes: a count stands for the shelf at the moment it is submitted, each line keeps the on-hand and movement sequence then, and its variance is counted minus that expected quantity, posted onto whatever is on hand when it posts, so movements during and after the count are kept, never undone. A shortage needs the reason lost or damaged and an overage found; a matched line needs none. Each posted variance is valued by PART-007 at the stock's average when it posts. The owner sets the approval threshold in USD: variances valued at or above it ($0.00, the default, means every variance) wait for a lead or the owner who did not count them, and smaller ones post at submission as the counter's movement. Approval is refused as stale once another count of that part has posted after the line was counted, and refused when posting would leave on-hand below zero; a rejection needs a reason and posts nothing. Each posted adjustment is a count movement attributed to the person who posted it, carrying its reason, value and count number, and is in the audit (ADMIN-006) and the period reconciliation (PART-007). Until stores roles exist (ADMIN-003) leads and the owner act for stores staff and the stores supervisor. Direct physical counts (GAS-03) stay as published. Done covers what exists today: one storeroom per site with shelf locations as text; PART-001 adds bins and bin counts, and ADMIN-003's storeroom clerk and stores supervisor inherit counting and independent approval, each before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Count a bin while another technician issues one unit, submit a variance and approve as the stores supervisor. Inspect reconciled expected balance, stale-count refusal and auditable quantity/value adjustments.

**PART-005 — Reorder points, lead time and automatic replenishment.** Leads set minimum/maximum, reorder quantity, safety stock, vendor and lead time per location. Crossing available-stock thresholds alerts stores, drafts a deduplicated requisition/PO and follows it until receipt; automatic ordering only uses a separately approved vendor/spend envelope. Open replenishment documents and their age appear in the stores report (PART-009).

Exactly: until PART-001 and ADMIN-002 add bins and sites, each part has one recorded stock location, and leads and the owner maintain immutable numbered policies for that location: minimum, maximum, reorder quantity, safety stock, active vendor, cost center, accountable active owner purchaser, calendar lead days and human-entered USD unit price, freight, sales/use tax and tax note. Available is on-hand less outstanding reservations; at or below minimum plus safety stock the quarter-hour worker drafts the larger of maximum minus available and reorder quantity, less outstanding linked deliveries, never below zero, with one open document per part. Read-only preview creates no purchases, notices, audit or execution rows. The draft pins its policy revision and creates an attributed in-app notice for the owner and leads; the notice is labelled stored in-app, with no external alert claimed. PM-005 inherits external email/push delivery before shipping it. Open documents show age as elapsed whole 24-hour days, exact remaining delivery and quarantine quantities, remaining stock shortage against maximum, and a due day equal to opening site-local day plus lead days; due on or before today prompts retained stores follow-up. Receipts and returns use BUY-004: quarantine is delivered but unavailable, and supplier returns reopen replacement shortage. Repeated workers neither duplicate the open document nor the same follow-up occasion. A buyer-edited PO revision is flagged for review rather than guessed to buy the same part. Automatic sending requires a separate immutable vendor/cost-center envelope proposed by the owner and explicitly approved by a different active owner or supervisor, never the policy author, envelope author, PO initiator or revision author. Its inclusive site-local period and per-order/period USD ceilings apply in addition to BUY-003 budgets; a claim consumes its amount even after uncertain or rejected submission, with no automatic retry or refund. The linked immutable PO vendor and cost center must match the current policy and envelope. Automatic sending also needs live BUY-003 threshold authority with no manual steps or emergency decision; otherwise the draft waits for ordinary independent purchasing decisions. Envelope ceilings and consumed USD amounts are visible only to the owner and supervisors with the review right, including in worker-history inputs; leads read vendor, cost center, dates and approval state and select an approved envelope by id without those amounts. Policy unit costs retain BUY-001/002 visibility. Revoking the envelope or ending its independent approver's authority stops new claims while retaining open orders. The owner pauses, previews, resumes and catches up under PM-008, and every automatic record keeps the worker job, grant revision and source facts; REPORT-009 defines the new measures and source doors. **Acceptance evidence:** Consume below minimum, run the replenishment worker twice, inspect one draft and delivered notice, approve within a spend envelope and receive a partial delivery. Inspect remaining shortage and due-date follow-up.

**PART-006 — Inter-site transfers and stock reconciliation.** Stores can request, approve, dispatch and receive transfers with in-transit custody and partial/lost quantities. Sender and receiver rights are separate; network replay never moves stock twice and count reports reconcile source, transit and destination. Open transfers and their age appear in the stores report (PART-009). **Acceptance evidence:** Transfer ten seals between sites, receive eight and mark two lost after approval, then replay delivery confirmation. Inspect source/destination/transit movements and variance cost without a second receipt.

**PART-007 — Inventory valuation and transaction history.** Parts retain purchase price, landed freight/tax allocation and a disclosed moving-average or FIFO policy. Work consumption snapshots its cost; later price changes and returns do not rewrite old asset cost. Owners can reconcile opening, movement and closing quantity/value.

Exactly: Gasket's disclosed policy is moving-average cost, kept in whole US cents, and every stock movement keeps its own signed value beside its quantity, so stock value is the sum of movement values and no later event rewrites one. A receipt is valued at its unit price times its quantity, rounded half up to a cent, plus the freight and sales tax entered on that receipt, landed wholly on its part; a receipt without a unit price takes the part's current vendor price, and with neither it is unpriced. An issue takes the stock's average (stock value times quantity over on-hand, rounded half up; the last unit out takes exactly what is left). A return credits the work order's own issued value for that part in the same proportion, never today's average, so a work order's parts cost is what its issues were taken at less what its returns credited. A count variance is valued at the average, or with nothing on hand at the latest priced receipt's landed unit cost, else $0.00. Setting or changing a part's vendor price (leads and the owner) revalues no stock and no work. The period reconciliation (JSON and CSV) covers site-local dates from and to, both included: per part, opening (every movement before the start of the first day), received, issued, returned, count adjustment and closing quantity and value, the average unit cost and the number of unpriced movements, with a total row; it is downloaded by the owner and by the leads and supervisors who download asset history and the ledger handoff (ASSET-007). Work orders show each part's consumed cost and the asset history shows each issue's and return's value. Movements recorded before valuation existed and moved-in opening stock carry no value and are counted as unpriced, never as a cost. Done covers what exists today (one storeroom per site and single-part receipts): PART-001 values stock per storeroom and bin, BUY-004 allocates one delivery's freight and tax across its lines before landing them, MIG-001 moves opening stock in with its source unit cost, and REPORT-001 carries these consumed and returned part values into work, asset, parent and site actual costs, each before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive two differently priced lots with freight and sales tax, issue/return units and change the vendor price. Download a period reconciliation and verify exact USD valuation and immutable historic work cost.

**PART-008 — Supplier catalogs and duplicate part control.** Parts support manufacturer/vendor numbers, unit packs/conversions, preferred and alternative suppliers, approved equivalences, photos and catalog prices. Proposed duplicate merges show all dependencies and preserve aliases/movements under an approved canonical item. Catalog CSVs name a stocking unit and the stocking quantity in one supplier pack; pack receipts multiply exact three-decimal quantities and refuse a result beyond three decimals, with USD extended pack prices rounded half up to cents. A repeated manufacturer number proposes a duplicate, never merges automatically. A lead or owner previews and approves a canonical item in the same stocking unit with a reason and the fingerprint of its dependencies; a changed preview, unfinished physical count or contradictory current BOM serial range is refused. A shelf count observed before a merge is stale even if the latest movement sequence is unchanged. Original part identities, movement quantities and values, receipts, kit and BOM revisions, aliases and photos remain retained; lookup of either old number opens the canonical item, whose balance combines their movements. The chosen canonical item supplies its shelf, minimum and current replenishment policy; source policies remain historical and all existing purchase documents still count against further replenishment. Catalog imports require a no-write review and exact source fingerprint, replay idempotently and retain source bytes, digest and attribution; undo removes only their changes and refuses later dependencies. **Acceptance evidence:** Import two supplier catalogs with each/box quantities and duplicate manufacturer numbers, preview and approve a merge, then scan either old number. Inspect correct conversion, compatibility and complete movement history.

**PART-009 — Stock performance and inventory history.** Stores report stockouts, demand by asset/work, slow/dead stock, turns, count accuracy, expiring lots and open replenishment/transfer age. Every number drills to movements and separates historical imports from current balances.

Exactly: the stores report (page, JSON and a source-movements CSV) is read by leads, supervisors and the owner over site-local dates from and to, both included (the last 90 days by default), and names its site. Stocked parts are those with stock on hand at some point in the period; a stockout is a movement in the period that leaves a stocked part with nothing on hand, each event naming that movement and its work order, and the stockout share is parts with a stockout over stocked parts; parts out of stock at the period's end are listed. Demand is issues less returns in the period, by quantity and the value PART-007 kept on them, per work order and per asset, with open reservations as committed demand. Slow stock is on hand at the period's end with no issue in the period; dead stock is on hand then with no issue in the 365 days ending then. Turns are issued less returned value over the average of opening and closing stock value, which are the PART-007 reconciliation's totals for the same period (two decimals, not annualized, none at a $0.00 average). Count accuracy is direct counts (GAS-03) and planned count lines (PART-004) in the period that found exactly the expected quantity, per part and in total. Opening stock moved in from MaintainX is listed apart from native receipts (part of balances, never of demand), every movement in the download is marked native or moved in, and moved-in work history costs stay in asset history, outside demand. Percentages have one decimal, rounded half up. Done covers what exists today (one site, replenishment documents, no controlled expiring lots or transfers): PART-003 adds expiring lots, PART-006 open transfer age and ADMIN-002 the site filter across sites, each to this report before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive, reserve, issue, count and age spare stock, then filter the stores dashboard by site and download source movements. Reconcile stockout and inventory value denominators with the same period.

**BUY-001 — Vendor records and maintenance requisitions.** Buyers manage US supplier contacts, ship-to addresses, tax treatment, payment terms, lead times, catalogs and active status. Technicians/planners request parts, services or repairs linked to work/asset/cost center, with an accountable purchaser and visible approval state.

Exactly: until ADMIN-003 supplies the buyer role, the owner acts as buyer and manages suppliers, catalog entries and cost centers; the owner, leads and maintainers submit requisitions, and existing internal members read the purchasing queue and supplier records. A supplier keeps its named contact, email and phone, US ship-to street/city/state/ZIP, recorded sales-tax, buyer use-tax or exemption treatment (an exemption needs its basis), payment terms, lead time in whole calendar days and active status. Catalog SKUs name a part, service or external repair, its unit and an optional quoted USD price in whole cents; an unknown price stays unknown. Supplier edits use numbered revisions and keep attributed before/after facts in audit. A requisition names an active supplier, active cost center and active owner as accountable purchaser, has part/service/repair lines with positive quantities exact to three decimals, and may link work, an asset, or both (then the work must belong to that asset); work supplies its asset when no asset is given. It keeps the supplier facts it requested against and shows Pending approval: it neither authorizes spend, sends an order nor receives stock. Disabling a supplier refuses new requisitions while retaining earlier ones. Done covers the current single site, roles and requisition door: ADMIN-002 adds site scope, ADMIN-003 buyer and purchasing rights, BUY-002 orders, BUY-003 independent spend approval and BUY-007 new external repair work, each inheriting active-supplier refusal for new purchasing before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a supplier and a technician requisition for bearings plus contractor labor, link the asset and cost center, and inspect the buyer queue. Disable the supplier and try to place new work against it.

**BUY-002 — Quotes and numbered purchase orders.** Buyers compare vendor quotations and draft sequentially numbered POs with quantities, units, USD prices, freight, US sales/use-tax fields, delivery dates, work/asset links and attachments. Sending records the exact approved revision and vendor acknowledgment separately.

Exactly: until ADMIN-003 provides the buyer role, the owner acts as buyer and existing internal members read quotes, orders and original attachments. Buyers record immutable supplier quotations and select among compared quotes with a reason, then save an order with a sequential PO number; every edit creates a new numbered immutable revision and invalidates any earlier approval for the new revision. Quantities are exact to three decimal places, USD unit prices are whole cents, each extended line rounds half up to a cent, and vendor payable is the sum of extended lines, freight and recorded sales tax; buyer use tax is shown separately and included in the disclosed commitment, never added to vendor payable. Tax treatment and exemption basis are human-entered, never a tax determination. A supervisor or a different owner approves the exact revision, never its initiator or revision author. With no eligible independent approver the PO page states that it is blocked and directs the owner to People and access to invite a supervisor; it offers no self-approval exception. BUY-003 adds budgets, multi-step limits, delegation and emergency override to this independent revision approval before it ships, including a threshold policy that may permit small orders to skip manual approval. The buyer submits the approved immutable snapshot and its attachments to its recorded vendor email through installation mail; one claimed send is retained per revision, including after a crash or uncertain result, and no replay automatically sends it again. Provider acceptance is labelled mailbox delivery unconfirmed; local development suppression says no vendor email was sent, and refusal or uncertainty remains visible. Vendor acknowledgment is a separately buyer-recorded contact, reference and note, labelled not independently verified, never inferred from provider acceptance. Disabling the supplier refuses new drafts, approvals and sends while retaining old versions, approvals, submission outcomes and acknowledgments. **Acceptance evidence:** Compare two quotes, draft a mixed parts/service PO, approve and send through vendor email, then revise quantity. Inspect numbered versions, totals, linked work and the requirement to reapprove changed spend.

**BUY-003 — Spend approval and purchasing separation.** Owners define per-site/cost-center budgets, dollar approval limits and multi-step approval/delegation. An initiator cannot approve their own purchase; currency, line or vendor changes invalidate approval. Emergency overrides require named authority and remain reportable. This clause extends BUY-002's exact-revision independent approval, invalidation on every edit and immutable send history with its budget, multi-step, delegation and emergency controls before it ships, including approval thresholds that may permit small POs to skip manual approval.

Exactly: until ADMIN-002 and ADMIN-003 add multiple sites and purchasing roles, the owner manages one site's policies and dated delegations, and active owners and supervisors supply independent decisions. A current immutable policy revision defines a USD budget for inclusive site-local dates, for the whole site or one cost center; both scopes apply together, and periods cannot overlap within one scope. The original authorization day books a commitment (threshold authorization books at send), never the promised delivery day. Required steps are the named active owner/supervisor at each threshold at or below the commitment, ordered by dollars, then site before cost center, then entered position; each earlier step must be approved first. A zero threshold asks for manual approval on every amount. Below every configured threshold, the policy supplies authority without manual approval, honestly labelled; with no policy, BUY-002's independent approval still applies. Delegation has inclusive dates, a reason and immutable versions: its delegate acts in place of its named principal, both must retain eligible roles and neither may be the initiator or current revision author. Each decision pins its policy step, delegation revision and exact PO revision, and policy or delegation changes are re-evaluated before later decisions and sending. Currency other than USD is refused without changing the order; line or vendor edits create a new revision needing authority again. Atomic budget checks count each approved current revision once and every sent historic revision until an independent reviewer explicitly confirms its release with a reason; an unsent superseded revision ceases to be an obligation. Neither competing completions nor send can exceed a ceiling without a separately confirmed independent emergency decision naming its authority, reason and projected budget impact. Releases and overrides remain in attributed reports and audit, and never assert receipt, supplier agreement, bill, posted actual cost or payment. Missing independent authority blocks with a page explaining how the owner adds a supervisor or changes its named policy/delegation. Existing internal members retain PO/history access with step names, status, delegates and outcomes; budget values and the override report require the owner or supervisor review right, and editing policies/delegations is owner-only. The versioned measure registry and source-linked report follow REPORT-009, including visible excluded/released obligations and unapproved drafts. ADMIN-002 adds site scoping, ADMIN-003 its buyer/approver grants, BUY-004 and BUY-005 actual receipts/bills and BUY-006 automatic-order limits before they ship; none changes this commitment into an invented actual. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a $4,500 PO across two approval limits, attempt self-approval, delegate during leave and change a line after approval. Inspect correct routing, renewed approval and separately reported emergency override.

**BUY-004 — Partial receiving, inspection and returns.** Stores match deliveries to approved PO lines, receive partially by bin/lot/serial, inspect/quarantine damaged goods and record backorders or supplier returns. Duplicate receipt identities do not add stock twice; remaining quantities stay open and receipts carry evidence. A delivery's freight and sales tax are allocated across its lines by line value before each line lands at its valued cost (PART-007).

Exactly: until ADMIN-003 supplies stores roles, leads and the owner receive and inspect; existing internal members read receipts and original evidence. Each delivery pins an approved immutable PO revision; a superseded revision may receive only after a retained send submission, and an unsent current revision must still have live authority. Part lines match an existing part in the same recorded unit; conversions are not inferred. A delivery may split a PO line across named bins, lots and individual serials; a serial identifies exactly one unit and is unique for that part. Delivered quantities are exact to three decimals and cannot exceed ordered quantity less prior deliveries plus supplier returns. Quarantine is delivered but excluded from usable stock and stock value until released after inspection. Attributed inspection events release held quarantine or return held quarantine or available usable goods to the supplier, with quantity and reason; returns reopen outstanding replacement quantities. Usable supplier returns remove current moving-average value as negative receipts, while quarantine returns remove only the held value; neither asserts a supplier credit, bill or payment. Each delivery keeps a supplier-scoped receipt identity: an identical replay returns the retained receipt, and a changed payload under that identity is refused. Original packing-slip bytes and SHA-256 remain downloadable behind sign-in. USD extended delivery lines round half up to a cent; freight and sales tax use largest-remainder allocation by delivered line value (ties by PO line position), then quantity splits within a line, and all allocated cents reconcile. A zero-value delivery cannot absorb nonzero charges. Quarantine takes its proportional landed value rounded half up, with the remainder retained on usable stock; releases exhaust the exact held remainder. The receiving page and JSON door show each revision's delivered, usable, quarantined, returned and outstanding quantities and retained backorder notes, with source-linked versioned definitions under REPORT-009. PART-001 carries bin-level stock, reservations and counts, PART-003 downstream controlled issues/expiry, and ADMIN-002 cross-site receiving scope before those capabilities ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive six of ten ordered parts, quarantine one, upload the packing slip and replay the receipt ID. Inspect five usable units, remaining order, quarantine/return movement and no duplicate quantity.

**BUY-005 — Bills, match exceptions and financial handoff.** Each received/partially received delivery can create a linked supplier bill. Buyers reconcile PO, receipt and bill quantity/price/tax, track credits and send approved bills/cost allocation to accounting. Payment status returns from the ledger; Gasket does not itself become a bank or general ledger. **Acceptance evidence:** Record two deliveries and bills, introduce a price/quantity mismatch, resolve under authorized tolerance and sync to QuickBooks Online. Replay and reverse a receipt; inspect one ledger bill per approved source and retained credit linkage.

**BUY-006 — Vendor delivery follow-up and replenishment control.** Buyers see promised/actual delivery, late items, acknowledgments and partial receipts; configured reminders chase the vendor and escalate a parts blocker to the planner. Auto-buy limits apply per order and period, and pausing a rule preserves open orders.

Exactly: until ADMIN-003 adds purchasing and planner roles, the owner acts as buyer and existing internal members read follow-up. The Vendor follow-up page and its JSON door follow each order's latest revision with a retained submission (accepted, locally suppressed, unconfirmed or uncertain; rejected, rate-limited and failed sends never reached the vendor and are not followed) and show its promised delivery day, each delivery's site-local day and receipt identity, the latest buyer-recorded acknowledgment (not independently verified) or none, and per line the ordered, delivered (quarantine included) and outstanding quantity, which is ordered less delivered plus supplier returns (BUY-004), exact to three decimals. An order is partly delivered while some but not all of it is delivered, and late while anything is outstanding and the site-local today is after its promised day, by whole calendar days; a completed order shows how many days after its promised day its last delivery came. Reminders run only under an owner-approved immutable numbered rule, none by default, and only while something is outstanding and the supplier is active: one acknowledgment reminder when no acknowledgment is recorded once the site-local days since the submission reach the rule's acknowledgment days (0 to 30), and one late reminder once the delivery is the rule's late days (1 to 30) past its promised day. Each is one email to the order's submitted vendor address through installation mail, claimed before submission and never resent, labelled with its provider outcome: provider acceptance is not mailbox delivery or vendor agreement, local development says no vendor email was sent, and uncertainty or refusal stays visible. A later submitted revision is followed afresh with its own occasions. A delivery that is the rule's escalation days (1 to 60) late with outstanding part lines while its linked work is still open is a parts blocker: one in-app escalation notice, linked to that work and the PO and shown in the work's chase, goes to the planners, who are every active lead (the owners when there is none); no external alert is claimed. The auto-buy limits are PART-005's independently approved envelopes: each caps every automatic order and the envelope's inclusive site-local period in USD, in addition to BUY-003 budgets, and an automatic order over either ceiling is not sent. Follow-up runs as PM-008's Vendor delivery follow-up job every quarter hour; the owner pauses, resumes and catches it up under its revision, the page and JSON door show exactly what the next run would do without writing anything, and pausing it or the replenishment job keeps every open order, its outstanding quantities and its records. Each reminder and escalation keeps its job, grant revision and rule number, the job keeps its input facts, and its measures follow REPORT-009. ADMIN-003 adds the buyer and planner roles, ADMIN-002 site scope and PM-005/INT-004 external delivery of escalations before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Send an approved PO, withhold vendor acknowledgment, advance past promised delivery and receive only part. Inspect vendor reminder, planner escalation, outstanding quantity and blocked overspend.

**BUY-007 — Contractor and external repair work.** Leads scope and authorize contractor work with quotes, service terms, qualification/insurance expiry, asset access window and expected costs. Contractors submit evidence, time/materials and invoices against scoped work; an independent supervisor accepts before costs are finalized. **Acceptance evidence:** Send a pump rebuild to a contractor with an expiring qualification, receive quote and completion evidence, return incomplete work, then accept and match its invoice. Inspect scoped access and actual cost in asset history.

**BUY-008 — Purchasing visibility and vendor performance.** Buyers report committed versus actual maintenance spend, open/late PO lines, approval age, vendor lead-time/quality and receipt/bill exceptions by site, asset and cost center. Reports link to original approvals, deliveries and posted financial IDs. **Acceptance evidence:** Draft, approve, partially receive and bill POs from two vendors, then download a monthly purchasing report. Reconcile commitments, actuals, late quantities and exception age to source documents.

**REPORT-001 — Work and asset maintenance costing.** Every work order and asset shows actual labor, consumed and returned parts, contractor, tool and miscellaneous USD costs alongside estimates, commitments and posted amounts. Parent, site and cost-center rollups avoid double counting and rate visibility follows role rights; parent roll-ups follow the asset hierarchy (ASSET-001). The repair cost entries leads record on work orders today (REPORT-005) are part of a work order's actual cost, and REPORT-005 ranks by this clause's reconciled work cost before it ships. Consumed and returned parts are the values PART-007 keeps on each issue and return, never a later price. **Acceptance evidence:** Complete a two-technician repair using parts and a contractor, return an unused part and reconcile work, asset, parent and site cost downloads with underlying approved entries. Open the downtime Pareto (REPORT-005) and see each failure's repair cost equal its work order's reconciled cost. Current implementation semantic (ct approved 23 October 2026): actuals add retained manual entries, signed consumed and returned PART-007 values, approved labor snapshots and captured contractor invoices, once per source. Existing manual entries stay additive because their external provenance is not guessed. Work, direct asset, current subtree, site and cost-center downloads share these sources; overlapping subtree rows are explicitly non-additive. Estimates, live approved purchase commitments, external commitment records and owner-recorded posted amounts are separate comparisons, never additional actual cost or verified ledger postings. Comparison corrections append a referenced credit; unknown source values and missing imported components remain disclosed. New financial comparison and work cost-center writes are owner-only; existing report readers retain aggregate USD access, without individual labor rates. REPORT-010 carries reconciled costs and approved time into its authorized PDF fields before it is done. BUY-005 and REPORT-008 inherit provider-confirmed bill and ledger reconciliation before shipping; ADMIN-002 and ADMIN-003 inherit current cost scopes and protected person-level rates.

**REPORT-002 — Downtime and production availability.** Report planned/unplanned outages, degraded operation, reason, failure mode, affected production window and availability denominator. Overlapping component events roll up without double counting; open outages and uncertain feed coverage remain visible with drill-down.

Exactly: the report covers a period of site-local days, both ends included (the last 30 days by default), for the site (every line and every entry with an outage) or one register entry and everything below it (ASSET-001), and is read by leads, supervisors and the owner. An outage is downtime recorded on a work order; whoever records it marks it a failure stop, a planned stop or degraded operation (the asset kept running at reduced output), with its reason and an optional failure mode, and its latest classification counts (REPORT-003). Outages are clipped to the period; one still open counts to now and its entry is listed as down now. Production time is the site's declared weekly production hours (windows per ISO weekday ending by midnight, which leads and the owner add and remove; with none declared, every hour of every day), as they stand now, inside the period; the source timeline shows each outage's recorded and clipped window, its work order and line, and its minutes inside and outside production time. An entry's planned time is the production time inside a planned stop of it or of anything below it, and is left out of the availability denominator (production time less planned time). Its down time is the denominator time inside a failure stop of it or of anything below it, overlapping outages counted once with the shared minutes shown, and availability is (denominator - down time) / denominator. Degraded operation is listed on its own, does not lower availability and is not a stop (REPORT-003). Unknown coverage is denominator time that no hour meter on the entry or below it was reporting (from its first to its last good reading in the period; a stale feed reading, ASSET-005, is not good), shown in hours and never estimated or counted as up or down. Minutes are whole; hours and percentages have one decimal, rounded half up. Done covers every source of outages and production time that exists today (downtime on work orders, declared production hours and hour meters); technician after-the-fact work FIELD-009, moved-in history MIG-001 and MIG-002, machine feeds INT-010 and INT-014, and production windows from PLAN-005 and INT-017 feed these definitions before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Enter overlapping component outages across a reporting boundary and a planned shutdown, then inspect asset/line availability and source timeline. Verify clipped windows, excluded planned time policy and explicit unknown coverage.

**REPORT-003 — MTBF, MTTR and failure analysis.** Reliability reports calculate MTBF from defined operating time and qualifying failure counts, MTTR from defined repair durations, and MTTA from acknowledgment events. Definitions, sample size, exclusions and unknown inputs are displayed; failure-code Pareto and repeat failures link to work.

Exactly: the report covers a period of site-local days, both ends included (the last 30 days by default), for the site or one asset, and is read by leads, supervisors and the owner. A stop is downtime recorded on a work order (degraded operation, REPORT-002, is not a stop); whoever records it marks it a planned stop or a failure, with an optional failure mode code (ASSET-004), and a lead or owner corrects that classification by appending a new one with a reason, never rewriting the stop or an earlier classification; the latest classification counts and every one stays visible with who and when. A qualifying failure is a stop that started in the period and is not classified as planned; planned stops are listed and left out of every measure. Operating time is what the asset's hour meter (a counter whose unit is h, hr, hrs, hour or hours; the first by name when there are several) counted between its first and last good reading in the period; the rest of the period is unknown coverage, shown in hours and never estimated. MTBF is operating hours divided by the failures that started inside that covered time; failures outside it, or on an asset without an hour meter, are excluded and counted. MTTR is the mean minutes from a failure's stop to back in service over failures that have ended; failures still down are excluded and counted. MTTA is the mean minutes from a failure's stop to the first acknowledgment of its work order (PLAN-002) at or after it; failures not acknowledged since are excluded and counted. The Pareto ranks failures by failure mode, most first, with each mode's share and the cumulative share, unclassified failures as their own row; a repeat failure is two or more failures of one asset with the same failure mode in the period. Hours, minutes and percentages have one decimal, rounded half up. Done covers every source of stops that exists today (downtime recorded on work orders); each later source of stops or operating time (technician after-the-fact work FIELD-009, moved-in history MIG-001 and MIG-002, machine feeds INT-010 and INT-014, parent and line roll-ups ASSET-001 and REPORT-002) records the same planned/failure classification and feeds these definitions before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Record three failures, one planned stop and missing operating coverage; compare MTBF/MTTR/MTTA and failure Pareto to hand-calculated source events. Correct a failure classification and inspect revised definitions and retained provenance.

**REPORT-004 — Backlog, PM compliance and schedule performance.** Leads see backlog age and estimated hours, overdue risk, PM on-time compliance, planned/reactive ratio, schedule attainment and work awaiting review. Missed/skipped/canceled PM occurrences remain in the disclosed denominator and drill to accountable work/blockers.

Exactly: the report covers a period of site-local days, both ends included (the last 30 days by default), for the site and optionally one team (a schedule may name a team and an estimate, which the work it issues carries). Backlog is open, in-progress and returned work now, by age since it was raised (0-7, 8-30, 31-90, over 90 days) with the leads' estimated hours, and work with no estimate is counted and named rather than guessed; overdue is due before today and at risk is due within the next 7 days and not started; work awaiting review is counted on its own. A PM occurrence is a schedule and its due date (when issued more than once, its latest work order counts) and is judged once its due date has passed or its work is done: on time when submitted on or before its due date, otherwise late, overdue (still open), canceled, skipped (an approved skip) or not generated (due with no work ever issued); all of these stay in the denominator, occurrences not yet due are left out and counted. Planned/reactive compares preventive and corrective work approved and closed in the period; schedule attainment is the share of work due in the period, judged the same way, done on or before its due date. Percentages have one decimal, rounded half up. **Acceptance evidence:** Create on-time, late, canceled and ungenerated PM obligations plus reactive repairs, then filter by site/team and compare counts/hours and compliance denominator against source due occurrences.

**REPORT-005 — Downtime Pareto and cost of bad actors.** Leads rank downtime by asset, line, failure mode and reason, alongside repeat failures, repair cost and documented lost-production assumptions. Unknown costs remain unknown; drill-down explains each ranked contributor and excludes duplicate component time.

Exactly: the report covers REPORT-002's period and scope (site-local days, both ends included, the last 30 days by default; the site or one register entry and everything below it) and is read by leads, supervisors and the owner. Ranked downtime is the production minutes (REPORT-002) of failure stops; planned stops and degraded operation are left out and counted. Where failures of an entry and of an entry above or below it overlap, the shared minutes count once, for the failure that started first (then the higher entry), and the other shows them as duplicate time; failures of unrelated entries are separate losses even at the same time. Leads rank by asset, by line (the entry's nearest line, or "No line"), by failure mode (the latest classification, or "Unclassified") and by reason (the recorded reason, ignoring case and outer spaces), most minutes first, each row with its share and the cumulative share of the ranked total, its repeat failures (as REPORT-003 defines them), its repair cost and its lost production, and a drill-down listing each contributing failure with its counted and duplicate minutes and its work order. Repair cost is the sum of the USD cost entries (parts, labor, contractor or other, each with a note) that leads and the owner record on the failures' work orders, each work order once per row; entries are never edited, a negative entry corrects earlier ones and a work order's total never goes below zero; a work order with no entry is unknown, never zero. Lost production is counted minutes times the documented USD rate per production hour of the failed entry or, when it has none, of its nearest entry above with one; leads and the owner document a rate with its basis, or document that it is unknown, and the latest one of an entry counts. With no rate, or a rate documented as unknown, the loss is unknown and never estimated. A CSV download carries every ranked failure's inputs (recorded and counted windows, production, counted and duplicate minutes, repair cost, the rate with its entry and basis, lost production) and writes "unknown" where nothing is documented. Money is USD in whole cents, rounded half up; percentages have one decimal. Done covers the cost and rate records that exist today; REPORT-001 makes its reconciled work cost this repair cost, and technician after-the-fact work FIELD-009, moved-in history MIG-001 and MIG-002 and machine feeds INT-010 and INT-014 feed failures through REPORT-002's definitions, each before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Enter costed failures across three assets, including overlapping components and one unknown loss rate, then inspect Pareto/cumulative percentages and exported inputs without a fabricated loss estimate.

**REPORT-006 — Scheduled reports and CSV PDF delivery.** Authorized users save report filters and schedule site-local email delivery of readable PDF and complete CSV datasets. Exports include definitions, period, freshness and permission scope; delivery failures are visible and restricted rates and files never leak to recipients. The current Settings door supports weekly Performance, Reliability, Availability, Downtime Pareto, asset history and stock valuation packs with saved team or asset filters where supported. Asset history requires one asset and retains period events with attribution and source references, excluding the asset detail document links. Valuation retains site-wide opening, movement and closing quantities and values with unpriced movement coverage; it refuses an asset filter. Each occurrence covers the seven completed site days before its delivery date. The saved site time zone survives later site setting changes. A repeated wall time uses its later occurrence; a missing wall time uses the first valid minute after the clock gap. Delayed execution handles one oldest outstanding occurrence per tick and retains each original reporting period. CSV uses typed scalar paths to retain every value and empty collection, with formula-safe cells; PDF retains readable report values and versioned definitions. Freshness, permission scope, source revision, source fingerprint, dashboard links and authorized site-wide data-quality context accompany the dataset.

Report delivery and assigned preparation policy: only active human owners create and authorize delivery schedules, with explicit audited consent and named active members. An owner may name one active human report reader as a delegated author for that schedule. Delegates can read and edit only their assigned schedules while the owning principal remains an active owner; every delegated edit is audited and forces a pause until an owner reviews and explicitly authorizes the saved revision. Delegates cannot grant authority, create independent schedules or resume delivery. Current report and export permissions, reassignment and ended access are enforced at schedule, draft, preview and download doors. Every recipient must currently have report and history-export access; the job rechecks the active owning principal, recipient role and saved revision after generation and immediately before sending one separate message per recipient. Original evidence files and individual labor rates are not included. A durable occurrence claim prevents automatic duplicate submission after retry or restart. The reserve, bounded by the prompt bytes and the output cap at the granted prices, is charged before the call and replaced by the cost from reported usage afterwards; a call that may have been billed but reported no usage keeps the whole reserve, shown as reserved, and a refusal before any work costs nothing. A run only prepares pending proposals as the agent identity, each citing records from its input; it cannot approve, spend, send or change work, and an answer outside the granted shape, scope or citations is refused with no proposal. Revoking permanently ends the grant, marks its running runs revoked, rejects the proposals those runs left pending and drops any answer that arrives later while still recording its cost; decisions already made stay. Every run keeps its grant revision, input versions, provider outcome, cost and basis, tokens, proposals with their human decisions and any measured outcome, and the export lists them without keys or provider text. Run cost and spend are ledger figures of recorded runs, not KPIs: any measure built on them is registered under REPORT-009 first. Runs are started by an owner, never by a schedule: a scheduled or event-started run inherits PM-008's preview, pause and health obligations before it ships, and AGENT-001, AGENT-002 and AGENT-005 through AGENT-008 inherit this grant, budget, scope and revocation for every model call they add (AGENT-007's retrieval of manuals also inherits the terms rule). **Acceptance evidence:** Grant a bounded reliability run with a dollar budget, inspect its data/action preview, approve one proposal and revoke during another run.
